# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.
- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — the generic challenge model this feature generalises.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.
- **Risk:** Challenge completion is currently in-memory/run-local; exposing it as a durable, replayable event (via the existing transcript/event infrastructure) is needed for reliable sync — mitigation: build the completion-event surface in the engine layer first.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module packaging complexity — reuse the approach validated by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam cloud saves, non-binary stat tracking, trading cards, and wishlist prompts are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the challenge→achievement layer be engine-generic (any game's challenges can map to Steam achievements, Main Street first) or only cover Main Street for now?" — Answer (user): "engine-generic". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: the layer is a core-engine module; Main Street is the first consumer.
- Q2: "When should the Steam sync be built?" — Answer (user): per the intake request, "when the steam version has been created these achievements should sync with Steam achievements." Implication: implementation of the Steam bridge is gated on the launcher + Steamworks items; the engine abstraction is not.
- OPEN QUESTION: The exact Steam achievement list/API names for the store backend (business/backend decision outside the repo) — the manifest defines them in one place; the store config must match.

# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.
- As a publisher, I want achievement give-aways delivered through the existing bundled-content/unlock architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Three games are selected** from the TCE catalog for achievement give-away; the selection is a documented business decision (Main Street is a noted candidate; selection avoids overlap with the follow-on-Steam bonus game choice — see Related work) and the chosen set + rationale is recorded in the item/design doc.
2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). Trigger definitions live in one config (achievement ids → game id) and are game-agnostic.
3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.

# Replace incident deck pre-ordering with runtime balanced card selection

## Problem Statement

The current incident deck uses `orderIncidentDeck()` to pre-order the entire face-down deck at build/reshuffle time using a soft-greedy algorithm. While this strongly favours repeat-spacing and streak constraints across the deck body, it can admit rare tail deviations when the pool is imbalanced, and the pre-arranged order changes the deterministic simulation in ways that are harder to predict and test (monte-carlo median widened from ~39.8 to ~153).

The fix: instead of pre-ordering, select each incident card **at runtime** from the remaining face-down deck pool, constrained by the resolved draw history. The deck remains face-down; only the selection mechanism changes.

## Users

- **Player (Main Street)**: Experiences fair, balanced incidents without visible deck manipulation — no card order visible, only the resolved sequence matters.
- **Developer/Tester**: Can reproduce deterministic game outcomes (same seed → same result) and reason about incident balance without tracking pre-order algorithms.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runtime selection**: `resolveIncident()` selects the next incident card at runtime from the remaining face-down pool using constraint-aware selection (`repeatSpacing` / `maxStreak`), instead of popping from a pre-ordered sequence. The deck is shuffled once at setup/reshuffle; cards are removed by index.
2. **Determinism preserved**: Same game seed produces the same incident draw sequence. The selection is fully deterministic (no RNG consumed during selection — constraints are evaluated against the pool order).
3. **Constraint compliance**: The same repeat-spacing (N) and max-streak (M) constraints from `IncidentBalanceState` are enforced at draw time using the existing tiered constraint relaxation (strict → relax-repeat → invariant-window → invariant-any → fallback).
4. **Reshuffle integration**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` shuffles remaining incident cards from the event deck/discards and then uses runtime selection (not pre-ordering) for subsequent draws.
5. **Full test suite passes**: Existing incident-balance tests are updated to reflect runtime selection; all Monte Carlo guardrails and regression tests pass.
6. **Documentation updated**: Code comments and docs (DEVELOPER.md incident-balance sections) reflect the runtime-selection mechanism, replacing pre-ordering references.

## Constraints

- Must keep seeded determinism — same seed produces the same draw sequence.
- Selection must consume no RNG (constraint evaluation is deterministic against deck order).
- Deck remains face-down and invisible to the player (UI unchanged).
- Backward compatibility with saved games must be maintained (existing saves use pre-ordered decks; deserialization should handle both formats).
- The existing `IncidentBalanceState` and `recordIncidentDraw()` must continue to work unchanged.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetCards.ts`**: Contains `orderIncidentDeck()` (pre-orders entire pool) and `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (runtime selection from a deck). Both use the same constraint tier system.
- **`MainStreetMarket.ts`**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at reshuffle time.
- **`MainStreetState.ts`**: `setupMainStreetGame()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at game start.
- **`MainStreetEngine.ts`**: `resolveIncident()` pops `incidentDeck.shift()` (pre-ordered card at front).
- **`tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts`**: Tests the current pre-order system via `orderIncidentDeck`.

## Desired Change

Replace `orderIncidentDeck()` with runtime selection using `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (or a refined variant). The flow becomes:

1. **Setup/reshuffle**: Gather incident pool → shuffle (seeded) → store as `incidentDeck`.
2. **Draw**: Call `findConstrainedIncidentIndex(deck, balance)` → remove chosen card by index → record draw with `recordIncidentDraw()`.

`findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists and implements the exact constraint logic needed. The change is to use it at draw time instead of pre-ordering.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Remove or deprecate `orderIncidentDeck`; `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Update `replenishIncidentDeck()` to shuffle-only (no `orderIncidentDeck`)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Update `setupMainStreetGame()` to shuffle-only for incident pool
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Update `resolveIncident()` to use runtime selection instead of `shift()`
- `tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts` — Update tests to reflect runtime selection; verify determinism

## Related Work

- **CG-0MSXOVQFL007G3VH** — Implement constraint-aware deck ordering (the pre-ordering system being replaced)
- **CG-0MSL0OP040043KKZ** — Incident Balance state (IncidentBalanceState, recordIncidentDraw, findConstrainedIncidentIndex)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Performance** — `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` scans the full deck each draw (O(N)). With ~60-80 incident cards, this is negligible.
- **Risk: Saved games** — Pre-ordered decks in legacy saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. Balance history drives constraints, not deck order.
- **Assumption:** `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` constraint logic is sufficient without modification. If the tier system needs refinement, that is tracked separately.
- **Scope guard:** This task replaces pre-ordering with runtime selection only. No changes to constraint thresholds, difficulty presets, or UI.
- **Opportunity (out of scope):** If runtime selection reveals new balancing insights, a follow-up task can tune `incidentRepeatSpacing` / `incidentMaxStreak` presets.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q**: Should we deprecate `orderIncidentDeck()` or keep it for legacy compatibility? — **Answer (Map)**: Deprecate and remove. The runtime selection approach fully replaces it. Any legacy code paths that reference it are internal and not exposed.
- **Q**: Does `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` need any modifications for runtime selection? — **Answer (Map)**: `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already returns the array index of the chosen card and works against a deck in the expected format. No modifications needed — it already implements the constraint tiers exactly as required.
- **Q**: How should saved games (which contain pre-ordered decks) be handled? — **Answer (Map)**: Saved game deserialization already handles the `incidentDeck → incidentBalance` migration. Pre-ordered decks in saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. No special handling needed — the balance history is the source of truth for constraints, not deck order.
data.risk: Low — findConstrainedIncidentIndex already implements the needed constraint logic; only wiring changes. Determinism preserved.

# Problem Statement

When a business card is upgraded (e.g., Bakery → Patisserie), the card's displayed name always shows the original business name ("Bakery") instead of the upgraded name ("Patisserie"). This is a visual bug that misrepresents the current state of the business on the street grid.

# Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want the upgraded business name to be displayed on the card so I can clearly see which version of the business I have.
- **As a player**, I expect the card to show "Patisserie" after applying the "Upgrade to Patisserie" card to my Bakery, not "Bakery" as it did before.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. When an upgrade is applied to a business card, the card's name — rendered as **part of the card image** (baked into the card SVG texture), not a Phaser overlay — reflects the upgraded name (e.g., "Patisserie" instead of "Bakery"). (Mechanism per manual review: "We want it to be a part of the card like the original name.")
2. The upgraded name is computed dynamically from the applied upgrade cards — no hard-coded name values on BusinessCard instances.
3. Multi-level upgrades display the name from the **most recently applied** upgrade (set in `displayName` each time `purchaseUpgrade()` runs).
4. Base (un-upgraded) cards display their original `name` as before — the name is already part of the card; no overlay shown.
5. The fix works for all business upgrade paths in the game (Bakery→Patisserie, Diner→Bistro, etc.)
6. Unit tests cover both base cards (no name overlay) and upgraded cards (upgraded name displayed as part of the card face). `upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` asserts `nameText` is removed; `card-svg-generator.test.ts` / `replaceCardTitleInSvg` cover the baked upgraded name.
7. All existing tests pass after the change.

# Constraints

- The `BusinessCard.name` field is `readonly` in the TypeScript interface — the fix must not make it mutable. A separate display-name mechanism is required.
- The display name must be pre-computed and stored on the BusinessCard during `purchaseUpgrade()` (`displayName` field), since the rendering path receives the BusinessCard, not the upgrade templates.
- The fix should be minimal: BusinessCard/UpgradeCard interface fields, `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()`, the SVG texture pipeline (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager`, `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator`), and removal of the `nameText` overlay (`UpgradeOverlaySpec`, `MainStreetRenderer`).
- The solution must be data-driven where possible (driven by CSV card data, specifically the `newDisplayName` upgrade column), not hard-coded logic.

# Existing State

- `BusinessCard` has a `readonly name: string` (original business name), `level: number` (upgrade level), `appliedUpgrades: string[]` (IDs of applied upgrades), and `displayName?: string` (upgraded name, set by `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()`).
- `UpgradeCard` has a `name: string` (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie"), `targetBusiness: string` (e.g., "Bakery"), and `newDisplayName?: string` (e.g., "Patisserie") from the CSV.
- Card data CSV column `name` on upgrade cards uses format "Upgrade to <new name>"; the `newDisplayName` column stores the business's new name directly.

# Desired Change

The upgraded name must render as **part of the card image**, exactly like the base name is part of the template SVG:

1. `BusinessCard.displayName?: string` — the current upgraded name, set by `purchaseUpgrade()`/`playUpgradeFromHand()` from the applied upgrade card's `newDisplayName` (most recent upgrade wins).
2. `generateBusinessCardSvg()` uses `displayName ?? name` for the baked card title.
3. The texture pipeline (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager`) produces **display-name variant textures**: upgraded street businesses request a texture keyed by template+displayName whose SVG face is the base template with the title replaced by the display name (`replaceCardTitleInSvg`), so the upgraded name is part of the card image.
4. Remove the `nameText` overlay from `UpgradeOverlaySpec` and `MainStreetRenderer.applyUpgradeOverlays()` — the name is no longer a Phaser text overlay.

# Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `BusinessCard.displayName`, `UpgradeCard.newDisplayName`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `purchaseUpgrade()` / `playUpgradeFromHand()` set `business.displayName`
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — upgrade cards carry `newDisplayName`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `generateBusinessCardSvg()` displayName title; `replaceCardTitleInSvg()` variant helper
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — display-name variant texture keys + generation + prewarm
- `src/ui/Renderer/adapters/MainStreetAdapter.ts` — thread `displayName` through card rendering
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — pass `displayName` to street/hand render sites; remove `nameText` overlay
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — remove `nameText` field
- `example-games/main-street/tests/` / `tests/main-street/` — unit tests

# Related Work

- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT**: Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (references patisserie upgrade in tutorial context).

---

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the BusinessCard.name field be updated, or should a separate display name mechanism be used?"
  - A: A separate display name mechanism is needed since `BusinessCard.name` is `readonly` and used for identification/logic elsewhere. The overlay should derive the display name from applied upgrades.
  - Evidence: TypeScript interface definition in `MainStreetCards.ts` line 234 (`readonly name: string`).

- Q: "Should the new name come from the upgrade card's name field, or a dedicated field?"
  - A: A dedicated field (`newDisplayName` on UpgradeCard) is preferred for clarity and to avoid fragile string parsing of "Upgrade to X" patterns.
  - Evidence: CSV data shows upgrade names as "Upgrade to Patisserie" — the new name is embedded but not cleanly extractable without parsing.

- Q (manual review, rgardler): "The updated label is still an overlay. We want it to be a part of the card like the original name."
  - A: The upgraded name is baked into the card's SVG texture as a display-name variant (see Desired Change), and the Phaser `nameText` overlay is removed.

AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

**Priority: High** | **Type: Task** | **Parent: CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP**

## Problem statement

`MainStreetAiStrategy` and `MainStreetMonteCarlo` must account for the new upgrade action costs. AI upgrade moves/plays need to consume the daily action budget deterministically per seed. Monte Carlo simulations must model upgrade actions with correct action cost semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `MainStreetAiStrategy` chooseUpgradeAction: evaluates upgrade moves/plays against remaining action budget. Does not propose upgrade action when `actionsRemaining <= 0`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade move-to-hand from hand counts as same-day composite (free) when applicable, costs 1 action when held from previous day.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade drag-drop model (if used) costs 1 action with +50% premium.
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo`: runSeed models upgrade actions with correct action budget semantics. Deterministic per seed — same seed produces same upgrade decisions.
- Monte Carlo strategy evaluation: upgrade actions scored against action budget constraints, no over-commitment of actions.

# Intake Brief: Main Street: npm run monte-carlo (tsx) fails on ?raw CSV imports

## Headline

`npm run monte-carlo` fails with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` because tsx cannot load the Vite-style `card-data.csv?raw` import; switch the affected npm scripts from tsx to vite-node (the verified, in-repo-precedented runner) and update docs per the Doc-Update Policy.

## Problem statement

Three npm scripts that transitively import `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, `save-load-smoke`) fail under tsx with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`. tsx's loader misparses the Vite `?raw` query suffix for non-TS/TXT extensions, treating the CSV as a JS module. Root cause is in the import chain (`MainStreetCards.ts` line 18: `import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`), not in the harness logic — the same harness runs correctly under vite-node.

## Users

- **Developer running balance validation** — "I want `npm run monte-carlo` to just work so I can verify card balance after rebalancing card-data.csv." Example story: after editing `card-data.csv`, a developer runs `npm run monte-carlo` (or `monte-carlo-sweep`) and gets the JSON + CSV outputs described in docs.
- **Developer running the save/load smoke check** — "I want `npm run save-load-smoke` to pass so I can quickly verify persistence round-trips." Currently it crashes with the same loader error before running any scenario.
- **Producer/CI reader** — wants the documented commands in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` to remain accurate and working.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run monte-carlo` completes successfully end-to-end with the default settings (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, greedy, maxTurns 25) and writes both JSON and CSV outputs; results are consistent with the verified working control run (200/200 runs; winRate 38.5%, medianScore 55.8, avgNoActionTurns 0 — i.e., determinism preserved, no balance drift).
2. `npm run monte-carlo-sweep` completes successfully in sweep mode (strategy × difficulty combinations) and writes its outputs.
3. `npm run save-load-smoke` completes successfully (exit 0, failures 0) — same root cause, same fix; expanded blast radius captured in this item.
4. Spot-check that unaffected tsx workflows still work (`npm run replay` or `balance-cards`) — no collateral regression from the runner switch.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, AGENTS.md scripts list, and docs/DEVELOPER.md, per the Doc-Update Policy; the vite-node rationale is documented in the same style as `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

## Constraints

- The npm script **names and CLI flags must not change** (`npm run monte-carlo`, `--seeds/--seed-prefix/--maxTurns/--strategy/--out/--csv-out`, `--sweep`, etc.) — the harness CLI is a documented interface.
- Testing/validation criterion preserved: seeded determinism must be maintained (same seed → same deal order → same outputs; no reliance on RNG ordering changes).
- Prefer the established runner pattern over bespoke tooling: **vite-node** is the in-repo precedent for scripts that import `MainStreetCards.ts` (see `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` already uses it for exactly this reason) and is verified working for both broken entry points. A custom tsx loader hook for `?raw` would work but is more complex, repo-specific, and has no precedent — evaluated and rejected as the primary path.
- Doc-Update Policy applies (package.json scripts change).

## Existing state

- `package.json` lines 17–18, 21: `monte-carlo` / `monte-carlo-sweep` = `tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts ...`; `save-load-smoke` = `tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` line 18 imports `./card-data.csv?raw` (Vite bundler syntax, docs comment: "bundled at build time via Vite's `?raw`").
- Import chains that break under tsx: `scripts/monte-carlo.ts` → `MainStreetMonteCarlo` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`; `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` → `MainStreetState` → `MainStreetCards` → `?raw`.
- Reproduced failures: `npx tsx scripts/monte-carlo.ts` and `npx tsx scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` both exit 1 with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` (Node v22.22.1).
- Verified working: `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/monte-carlo.ts --seeds 200 ...` (200/200; winRate 38.5%) and `node_modules/.bin/vite-node scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` (failures 0).
- Tests are unaffected — vitest handles `?raw` via Vite (e.g. `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`).
- Pre-existing: reproduced at commit b2bec26b (before CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA F1–F4) and at HEAD.

## Desired change

Switch `monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`, and `save-load-smoke` package.json scripts from `tsx` to `vite-node` (entry scripts stay unchanged). Update docs per the Doc-Update Policy (AGENTS.md scripts list, docs/DEVELOPER.md; add the vite-node rationale for MainStreetCards-importing scripts in the same style as card-catalog.md). No engine or game code changes expected.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — scripts lines 17–18 (`monte-carlo`, `monte-carlo-sweep`) and 21 (`save-load-smoke`): tsx → vite-node.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — root cause location (`import cardDataRaw from './card-data.csv?raw'`); likely unchanged, but should be re-verified and its "bundled at build time" comment cross-referenced.
- `scripts/monte-carlo.ts`, `scripts/save-load-smoke.ts` — entry points; unchanged, but verification targets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (lines ~197, ~230), `AGENTS.md` (scripts list, line ~76) — doc updates per Doc-Update Policy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (line 67) — precedent/template for documenting the vite-node rationale.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT4RBCE2001DVCY — DUPLICATE** (status open): identical description, created 7 seconds earlier — a double-submit of this item. Producer to resolve (likely close in favour of this item, CG-0MT4RBHQR006C5GR).
- CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW — "Monte Carlo sanity-check and full-suite verification" (open, in_progress): the discovering item; this bug was found while verifying it. `discovered-from` relationship already recorded.
- CG-0MT3J8FXG006RCOA — "Main Street: reputation score multiplier" (in_progress, plan_complete): commit b2bec26b predates this work; bug reproduced before and after it (pre-existing, not a regression of that item).
- CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY — "Replay CLI tests ... (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm ...)" (completed): related tsx CLI tooling context.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — documents the vite-node precedent for scripts importing `MainStreetCards.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (approach):** vite-node is the chosen fix over a tsx `?raw` loader hook — based on in-repo precedent (card-catalog.md), verified success on both broken scripts, and lower maintenance surface. If the producer prefers the loader-hook approach, scope is limited to the monte-carlo/save-load-smoke invocations and the doc updates shrink accordingly.
- **Assumption (scope):** fixing `save-load-smoke` in the same item is in-scope — same root cause, same fix, verified working under vite-node. If the producer wants to split it, create a child item.
- **Risk:** switching runners could subtly change module resolution for other `@alias` imports in the chain — mitigated by the verification ACs (output parity with the control run; full test suite) and by the existing precedent (vite-node already used for a MainStreetCards-importing generator).
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to harness logic, balance logic, or CSV handling are in scope; any balance-tuning opportunities surfaced by the working harness are separate work items (see CG-0MT47FBLS000E7PW).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Interview-driven questions were not required — the seed context (goal, confirmed working path, likely fix options) plus repo verification sufficed to draft the brief. Decisions recorded for auditability:

- Q: "Fix via vite-node or a custom tsx loader hook?" — Answer (research, no user input needed): **vite-node**. Evidence: `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` line 67 explicitly documents vite-node for `generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` "(uses Vite-aware ESM loader because it imports deck-building functions from MainStreetCards.ts)" — the identical situation; both broken entry points verified green under vite-node. Loader-hook alternative has no precedent and higher maintenance; recorded as evaluated-and-rejected.

Included in ACs as in-scope via same-fix. `replay`, `export-transcripts`, `run-balance-cards` verified unaffected (no `?raw` chain).

# Converting coins/reputation should consume an action (CG-0MT5UPQGX005GWRP)

## Problem Statement

The Community Favour exchange (coins ↔ reputation) currently only enforces a once-per-turn gate via `favourUsedThisTurn` but does not consume a daily action. Other market actions (buy business, hire staff, buy event, peek incident deck, etc.) all consume one action via `consumeAction(state)`. Community Favour is inconsistent with this economy.

## Users

- **Main Street players**: When they click "Community Favour" to exchange coins for reputation or vice versa, it should count as one of their daily actions — the same as buying a business or hiring staff.
- **Tutorial players**: The tutorial scenario expects Community Favour to be an action-gated choice; without action consumption the economy and tutorial flow are inconsistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Community Favour consumes one action**: Calling `executeAction(state, { type: 'community-favour', direction })` must call `consumeAction(state)`, decrementing both `actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions`.
2. **ActionsRemaining is decremented in the engine test**: The existing test `'does not decrement actionsRemaining'` in `tests/main-street/community-favour-engine.test.ts` must be updated to assert `state.actionsRemaining` is decremented by 1.
3. **Once-per-turn gate still works**: The `favourUsedThisTurn` flag continues to prevent a second Community Favour exchange in the same turn (this is additional to action consumption — a player with actions remaining still can't double-exchange).
4. **No actions remaining → illegal**: If a player has no actions left (`actionsRemaining <= 0`), calling `executeCommunityFavour` must throw an error (via `consumeAction`'s guard) before any resource changes occur.
5. **AI strategy respects action consumption**: Community Favour AI decisions must still respect the action budget — the AI strategy should not attempt Community Favour when no actions remain.
6. **All existing tests pass**: The full Main Street test suite (unit + browser) passes after the change.

## Constraints

- The fix is minimal: one line addition in `executeCommunityFavour()` — `consumeAction(state)` before `state.favourUsedThisTurn = true`.
- The existing once-per-turn gate (`favourUsedThisTurn`) must remain — action consumption and once-per-turn are two separate guards.
- The existing test that asserts "does not decrement actionsRemaining" must be flipped to assert it does.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `executeCommunityFavour()` (line ~735) does not call `consumeAction(state)`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: All other actions in `executeAction` switch call `consumeAction(state)` (move-to-hand, buy-business, hire-staff, buy-event, peek-incident-deck, etc.).
- `MainStreetTurnController.ts`: `onCommunityFavourClick()` checks `favourUsedThisTurn` as a guard but relies on the engine for the actual action.
- `tests/main-street/community-favour-engine.test.ts`: Contains a test `'does not decrement actionsRemaining'` that asserts the current (incorrect) behaviour.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `consumeAction(state)` call in `executeCommunityFavour()`
- `tests/main-street/community-favour-engine.test.ts` — Update the test that asserts actionsRemaining is not decremented; add a test that verifies it IS decremented
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — No changes needed (command layer already delegates to engine)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — May need verification that AI respects action budget for Community Favour decisions

## Related Work

- **CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET** — Implement Community Favour mechanic (original implementation)
- **CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC** — Action economy enforcement (shared `consumeAction` helper)
- **CG-0MT2473A500839A0** — Tutorial: Community Favour step

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: This is a focused one-line fix. Any additional Community Favour improvements (e.g., UI button disable timing, tutorial gating) should be tracked as separate work items.
- **Assumption**: The AI strategy already checks action availability before Community Favour — if not, the AI test file (`tests/main-street/community-favour-ai.test.ts`) may need a new test.
- **Assumption**: Tutorial flow does not expect Community Favour to be "free" — the tutorial scenario should be reviewed if it performs Community Favour multiple times per turn.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No questions required — the issue is clear from the codebase and the work item description.

# Main street arcade should not be a service bridge

**Type:** Bug | **Priority:** High | **Assignee:** Map

## Problem Statement

The Arcade (`biz-arcade`) is currently a **Service bridge** — its synergy types are `Entertainment|Service`, so it earns adjacency bonuses from, and grants bonuses to, both Entertainment and Service neighbours. An arcade is purely an entertainment business ("retro fun for all ages"); it should be Entertainment-only and must not function as a Service business. The bridge designation was an artificial balance lever (CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB stretched T3 to two synergy types via this bridge), and it is thematically wrong.

## Users

- **Players** — an arcade alongside a laundromat or hardware store earning Service synergy feels wrong; the game's adjacency bonuses should match the business's real-world identity.
- **Designers/balance** — a correct, defensible per-tier synergy composition documented in `card-data.csv` and the docs; balance regenerated without distorting card identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Arcade becomes Entertainment-only:** `biz-arcade` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has `synergyTypes = Entertainment` (no `Service`); its `description` no longer claims a Service bridge and matches the Entertainment single-type template used by Cinema/Music Store.
2. **T3 stays balanced — a second card carries the non-Entertainment type:** exactly one additional card is added or retagged into T3 (producer directive: option (b)) so T3 still spans ≥ 2 distinct synergy types and satisfies the ≤2× per-tier balance rule from `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` (e.g. moving Community Shelter `cs-shelter` Service T6→T3 keeps T3 at `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}`, leaving the existing T3 snapshot unchanged; a viable alternative is adding a new Service card at T3).
3. **No other tier regresses:** after the change, every tier 1–12 with synergy-bearing cards still spans ≥ 2 distinct types with no type exceeding 2× any other (the `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` rule must still pass for all tiers; its `retagged/bridged cards carry the expected synergy types` assertion is updated so `biz-arcade` = `['Entertainment']` only).
4. **Tests:** `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` updated (Arcade assertion; T3 snapshot adjusted only if the chosen card changes the composition); any other affected tests (e.g. `group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` if `cs-shelter` is moved) updated; full suite `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
5. **Docs updated in the same commit:** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (Arcade catalog row; Service bridge list drops Arcade — currently 3 bridges listed; Service/Entertainment type-coverage tables) and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (per-tier synergy model notes) reflect the change, per the doc-update policy.

## Constraints

- No `synergyTypes` added to cards that currently have none (standing constraint from CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB).
- Retagging/relocation acceptable where flavour-sensible; a new card is allowed if no retag fits, but additions stay minimal (cost ladder and tier economy apply — T3 new-card cost should sit in the cost-4 band like Arcade/Laundromat).
- Flavour preserved: the Arcade stays Entertainment; Playground remains Entertainment (it is a park-type amenity).
- No dedicated SVG needed if the chosen fix moves an existing card (no pool-size change ⇒ no seeded RNG shift); adding a new card requires the SVG pipeline run and shifts seeded draws (precedent CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).

## Existing state

- `biz-arcade` row (CSV): cost 4, baseIncome 2.9, tier 3, `Entertainment|Service`, rep +0.05/turn, desc "Retro fun for all ages. Bridges Entertainment and Service synergies."
- T3 currently: `biz-arcade` + `cs-playground` (Entertainment) ⇒ synergy counts `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}`; this exact snapshot is asserted in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`.
- The Arcade bridge was introduced by CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB to stretch T3 (which otherwise had only Playground=Entertainment and was single-type); its rationale is recorded in test comments and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` ("Entertainment→Service bridge so T3 spans two types; an arcade is an entertainment service").

## Desired change

2. Rebalance T3 per option (b): move `cs-shelter` T6→T3 (recommended — restores `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}` in T3 with zero pool-size change, keeps T6 at `{Service: 1, Commerce: 1}`, keeps cs-tier count ≥ 6, and a shelter is thematically a neighbourhood amenity) **or** add a new Service card at T3 (cost 4) — implementer choice, documented with a balance rationale in the work item and updated Help Panel/description text as needed.

4. Update `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Arcade synergy/description; T3 second card (relocated or new).
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — Arcade assertion (`['Entertainment']`); T3/T6 snapshots if composition changes.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — cs-shelter tier assertion (if Shelter is moved).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — uses Arcade in market/synergy scenarios (verify no assumption of Service pairing).
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — catalog rows, synergy-coverage tables, bridge lists.
- `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — only if a new card is added.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB** (completed) — synergy-type rebalance that *introduced* the Arcade Entertainment|Service bridge; origin of the current design and the `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` rule.
- **CG-0MSQJ1XIB0004QVN** (completed) — Group A business cards including bridge design contract (implementers tune numbers only with documented rationale).

- **CG-0MT3C744B009DS84** (completed) — 12-tier expansion; T3 = "Neighborhood" (rep 8).

- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — seeded determinism precedent for pool-size changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption — option (b) scope:** moving an existing card into T3 is preferred over a new card (no SVG/pool change, no seeded-RNG shift, no cost-ladder expansion). Community Shelter is the candidate; if the implementer finds its T3 placement unbalanced, a new Service card at cost 4 is the fallback — flagged as an Open Question only if neither works.
- **Assumption — T3 composition target:** {Entertainment: 2, Service: 1} (via Arcade + Playground + Service) mirrors today's snapshot so the min change is a single relocated card; any deviation must keep the ≤2× rule.
- **Scope-creep guard:** tuning Service counts in other tiers, adding cards beyond the single T3 slot, or re-running a full synergy rebalance are NOT in scope — record as separate work items.

If the Arcade becomes Entertainment-only, T3 would be single-type and violate the ≤2× balance rule. Intended resolution? (a) Accept single-type T3 / (b) Add or retag another card into T3 / (c) Move a different card to T3 / (d) Other" — Answer (producer, interactive reply to `/skill:intake`): **(b) Add or retag another card into T3 to provide a second synergy type.** Research: T3 currently holds only Arcade + Playground (both Entertainment); a second card carrying Service (moved Community Shelter or a new Service card) restores `{Entertainment: 2, Service: 1}` without disturbing other tiers.

# Intake Brief: In main street log should show total effects

**Work item:** CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ · type `feature` · priority `high`

**Headline:** The Main Street Activity Log will show the complete effective
(post-mitigation) coin and reputation effects of every action — not just
costs — and a per-turn net summary row, so players can see the total impact
of what they did.

## Problem statement

The Main Street Activity Log records only partial information per action — for
example, playing an event card from hand logs how much it cost but not the
revenue/reputation impact it caused, and there is no aggregate of a turn's net
resource change. Players cannot see the complete (total) effect of their actions
from the log.

## Users

- **Player** — wants to understand, from the activity log, the full effect of
  each action (cost, coin delta, reputation delta) and the net resource change
  per turn, without cross-checking the resource bank themselves.

User stories:

- "As a player, when I play an event card, I want the log to show both its cost
  and its effective coin/reputation impact so I can see what it did."
- "As a player, at the end of each turn I want a summary line showing the net
  coin and reputation change for that turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Full effects on all resource-mutating entries.** Every action that
  changes coins and/or reputation produces a log entry showing its effective
  (post-mitigation) coin and/or reputation deltas alongside the existing
  action-specific text (cost, name, slot, etc.). Coverage: play event from hand,
  business purchase, community-space purchase, buy-and-place (incl. premium),
  upgrade purchase, sell (hand & slot), community favour exchange, re-roll
  market, staff hire/layoff, staff & ongoing costs, income phase, incident
  resolution, and any other resource-mutating action currently logged with
  partial information. Deltas are computed as the actual change applied to the
  resource bank (post staff buffs, Brand Ambassador multiplier, reputation
  multiplier — consistent with the existing `describeEventEffects` pattern).
- **AC2 — Played-from-hand event entries.** `playEventFromHand` logs cost plus
  effective deltas (e.g. `Played event X from hand (-€5 cost, +3 coins, +2 rep)`),
  matching the format incidents already produce; classification uses the net
  coin+rep effect (not raw cost).
- **AC3 — Per-turn net summary row.** A single aggregate entry such as
  `Turn N net: +12 coins, +1 rep` is appended at the end of each turn's
  end-of-turn processing, summarizing that day's net coin/reputation change
  (day-start snapshot vs. end-of-turn values). Emitted even when the net is
  zero; defined behaviour when the game ends prematurely (e.g. emitted before
  the game-over entry, or suppressed — chosen by the implementer and covered by
  tests).
- **AC4 — No regression in log readability/mechanics.** Entries remain one line
  where possible (word-wrap already supported); gain/loss/neutral colouring
  remains sensible; scroll/auto-scroll behaviour in `refreshLog` is unchanged
  for the existing entry count handling.
- **AC5 — Tests and docs.** `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` extended
  to assert the enriched entries and the per-turn net row; any existing tests
  asserting old entry text are updated; browser log-rendering tests still pass.
  "All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries."
  "Full project test suite must pass with the new changes."

## Constraints

- Effective (post-mitigation) values only — never raw card values — so the log
  matches what the player actually gained/lost.
- Reuse/extract the existing effect description helpers
  (`describeEventEffects`, `classifyEffect` in `MainStreetEngine.ts`, currently
  private) rather than duplicating formatting logic.
- Log lines stay compact (panel ~300px wide, scrollable); no unbounded text.
- The day-start snapshot needed for the net row must survive save/load and
  replay (include in `MainStreetState` clone/restore/serialization or be
  recomputable from logged data).
- Undo (command snapshots in `MainStreetCommands.ts`) already capture
  `activityLog` wholesale — new entry shapes must remain cloneable there.

## Existing state

- `LogEntry { turn, text, type }` appended via `addLog()`; rendered by
  `MainStreetRenderer.refreshLog()`.
- `playEventFromHand` (MainStreetMarket.ts ≈L603-619) logs
  `Played event X from hand (-€X)` and always classifies 'loss'.
- Incidents (`resolveIncident`), `playHeldEvent`, and `resolveHeldInvestment`
  already log effective deltas via `describeEventEffects` (e.g.
  `Incident: X (+3 coins, +2 rep)`).
- Partial entries elsewhere: purchases log cost only; sells log +coins only;
  income phase logs +coins (+rep as separate lines); duration events log their
  multiplier text.

## Desired change

Each resource-mutating action logs its effective coin/reputation deltas (in
addition to existing text), event cards played from hand are brought in line
with incidents, and a per-turn net summary row is appended at end of turn.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — enrich `playEventFromHand`,
  `purchaseBusiness`, `purchaseUpgrade`, buy-and-place, sellFromHand/SellFromSlot,
  move-to-hand, re-roll log entries.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — expose/reuse
  `describeEventEffects` + `classifyEffect` helpers; enrich community favour,
  layoff, staff/ongoing-cost, incident entries; add per-turn net row in
  `processEndOfTurn`; day-start snapshot in `executeDayStart`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — income/rep/from-cards
  entries (already mostly complete; verify coverage of negative-income cases).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — possibly shared helper
  exports and/or net-row snapshot fields (clone/restore).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — sell-dialog log
  entry enrichment.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` — extend for new formats + net row;
  update tests asserting old text.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** entry classification continues to use the existing
  `classifyEffect` net coin+rep heuristic (gain/loss/neutral), per Q2.
- **Assumption:** the structured transcript recording
  (`recordMainStreetEvent`) is unchanged — this item only alters the
  human-readable log text and adds the net row.
- **Risk (readability):** richer entries could make lines long in a ~300px
  panel. Mitigation: compact formatting (reuse `describeEventEffects` style),
  keep existing substrings (name, slot, €cost), word-wrap already supported.
- **Risk (test churn):** many existing tests assert old entry text. Mitigation:
  additive formatting where possible and update assertions in the same change;
  full suite must pass (AC5).
- **Risk (net row edges):** early game-over/early-return paths in
  `processEndOfTurn` and save/load/replay must handle the snapshot
  (serialization or recomputation) — covered by AC3/Constraints.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "all actions" is bounded by the explicit coverage
  list in AC1; any action type found to need richer logging during
  implementation becomes a follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `CG-0MT5VXSSQ003O5ZC` — "Remove 'Market cycled...' activity log" (open) —
  adjacent log-content change; keep separate.
- **CG-0MM8RCXD511MYXZU** (completed) — reorganised the investments row /
  incident queue / player hand; defines where event-play logging lives.
- **CG-0MM8PGEIK14423LQ** (completed) — updated tests for the
  Investment/Incident rename and held event mechanics; migrated the interactive
  event path to `playEventFromHand`, whose log entry this item enriches.
  (CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X 'Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility' also surfaced by
  automation — unrelated; ignored.)
- Completed log-mechanics items: `CG-0MQK4H9180049050` (scroll off top),
  `CG-0MQQHBHHV0000UNG` (container overflow), `CG-0MMLDBB070D8LO7T` (second
  game blank log), `CG-0MQQHBY72007PZPC` (reduce height) — content is
  unchanged by this item.
- In-repo precedent for effective-delta logging: incident/held-event entries
  via `describeEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngine.ts`).
- Docs touched by related automation: `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`,
  `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` (check for log-format
  specs when updating docs per AC5).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Scope:** "The description says the log should show 'the total effects of
all actions', with the event card as the example. Should this item (a) enrich
the whole log (every action type), or (b) focus on event entries first, leaving
other action types as follow-up work items?"
**Answer** — "all" (user). Final scope: enrich the whole log (option a).
Source: interactive reply. Research: all resource-mutating entries were
audited; incidents already log effects, making event-play the most visible gap,
but purchases/sells/favour etc. are also partial.

**Q2 — Event entry format:** "For a played event, should the entry show cost
plus the effective (post-mitigation) deltas, e.g.
`Played event X from hand (-€5 cost, +3 coins, +2 rep)` — consistent with the
existing incident format? Should the 'loss' classification consider the net
coin+rep effect rather than the raw cost?"
**Answer** — "post-mitigation deltas" (user). Final decision: show cost plus
effective post-mitigation deltas; classification follows the existing
`classifyEffect` net coin+rep heuristic (assumption documented in this brief).
Source: interactive reply. Research: `describeEventEffects`/`classifyEffect`
(MainStreetEngine.ts:347-364) already implement both behaviours for incidents.

**Q3 — Turn totals row:** "Does 'total effects' also mean a per-turn aggregate
row (e.g. `Turn 3 net: +12 coins, +1 rep`) summarizing all resource changes
that turn, or strictly per-action entries only?"
**Answer** — "yes" (user). Final decision: add the per-turn net summary row
(AC3). Source: interactive reply. Research: `processEndOfTurn`
(MainStreetEngine.ts:962) is the natural emission point; a day-start snapshot in
`executeDayStart` (L917) provides the baseline; `MainStreetState` clone/restore
must carry any new snapshot fields.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM8PGEIK14423LQ** – Update all tests for Investment/Incident rename and held event mechanics (completed)
- **CG-0MSRKN325004ELH2** – Review optimal pass values for avgCoinsPerTurn, winRate, medianScore (completed)
- **CG-0MLSW8TKZ0YHXJR2** – Investigate and fix broken Golf UI interactions (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: action, actions, actual, actually, add (+304 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actual, actually (+240 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: action, actions, actual, actually, add (+235 more)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)
