## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a competitive state model with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score plus owner-tagged street slots, so the shared street can host multiple owners deterministically via seeded RNG.

## Context

MainStreetState is single-player only (single resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining/finalScore and 10-slot streetGrid of BusinessCard|null). No owner concept exists. This child is the foundation for all competitive layers. Design is parallel per-player (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner, N-player-ready — not a hardcoded 2-player shape, not a single-player shim per producer decision “latter”). The game remains playable without an AI — competitive state is additive; single-player flow is preserved as the 1-player case (N=1).

## Scope

- Introduce per-player state: PlayerRecord (coins, reputation, hand, staff, actionBudget, score) × N; owner-tagged StreetGrid slots (ownerId per slot, null = empty).
- Deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG (same seed → same initial deal).
- Market/decks/incidentDeck remain shared; challenges/activeEffects remain game-scoped unless a rule explicitly scopes them.
- No AI, no income routing, no phase alternation — those are siblings.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling).
- Shared-day phase machine (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo (siblings).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 deferred child).
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue per producer decision).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** State type exposes per-player resources (coins/reputation), hand, staff, action budget, and score per owner plus owner-tagged street slots; setup creates a deterministic initial state from a seed.

# Intake Brief: Add a dev mode cheat to add a specific card to the market (CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5)

**Priority: Critical** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Add a dev-mode debug tool that lets a tester replace a random current market card with any card in the Main Street pool. Entry is a button in the Settings panel Debug Tools section (visible only under `import.meta.env.DEV` via the existing `DebugToolsEntry`/`CardGameScene` debug-tools framework). Selecting a card via mouse or keyboard (arrow keys + Enter) performs the replacement and refreshes the market display.

## Problem Statement

Debugging Main Street gameplay that depends on specific market cards (business, community space, event, upgrade, or staff) is slow without a way to force a desired card into the 3-card single-row market. A dev-mode cheat that replaces a random market card with a chosen card will make it possible to reproduce and validate edge cases (progression gating, deck composition, economy constraints, synergy adjacency, and staff-skill assignment) on demand without manipulating saves or seeds.

## Users

- **Engine / game developer debugging Main Street:** Needs to force a specific business, community-space, event, upgrade, or staff card into the market to reproduce layout, synergy, or gating bugs.
  - *"As a developer, I want to open a card picker from the Debug Tools section and inject a chosen card into the market so I can reproduce a synergy or tier-gating scenario in one click."*
- **QA / manual tester validating progression and balance:** Needs to exercise rare or tier-gated cards without grinding through many refreshes or seeded deals.
  - *"As a QA tester, I want to search the full card pool by name and add a specific card to the market so I can verify its interactions without waiting for it to appear naturally."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev-mode gated Debug Tools entry:** A button/entry appears in the Settings panel Debug Tools section only when running under `npm run dev` (`import.meta.env.DEV === true` via the existing `isDevMode()` / `SettingsPanel` `debugTools` / `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` framework). In production builds the entry and its code are absent / tree-shaken and the production bundle does not expose the feature.

- **Card picker window on activation:** Clicking the debug entry opens a window/panel that lists **all cards in the game** (all Main Street card families — Business, Community Space, Event, Upgrade, Staff) derived from the live card template registry (`getBusinessTemplates()`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()`, `getEventTemplates()`, `getUpgradeTemplates()`, `getStaffCardTemplates()` / `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` in `MainStreetCards.ts`), respecting the currently loaded CSV (`getCsvRows()` / `loadTemplatesFromCsv` reload path).

- **Grouped + filtered presentation:** The picker groups cards by type/family and provides at least (a) a type filter (select one or more families) and (b) a text box that filters by partial title match (case-insensitive substring against the card display name). Filters compose (type ∩ text); clearing filters shows the full grouped list again.

- **Mouse and keyboard selection:** A card can be selected by mouse click **or** by keyboard (arrow keys to move focus/selection, Enter to confirm). The picker is operable without a mouse.

- **Replace a random market card:** Confirming a selection replaces a **random** card among the **currently available market cards** (`state.market.cards`, length `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS === 3` in `MainStreetCards.ts` / `MainStreetState.ts`) with the chosen card. The random choice is uniformly over the current market slots; the market row is re-rendered immediately and the game state remains valid (no duplicate-id corruption — the injected card receives a distinct instance `id`; if the source template holds multiple copies, one fresh instance is created). The displaced card is returned to its family's discard/deck per the existing Main Street market lifecycle (do not lose cards).

- **Non-destructive and reversible via existing flows:** The replacement does not corrupt save/load (versioned serialization), transcript recording, undo/redo, or tutorial scenario state; subsequent market refreshes/cycling continue to use the normal deck/discard pipelines. If a nicer UX is needed, the operation may be wired as a command so undo returns the market to its prior composition (nice-to-have, not required).

- **Testing — unit tests:** Unit tests cover: dev-mode gating of the tool, picker filtering/grouping logic (type filter + text search), keyboard navigation, and the market-replacement effect (random slot replacement, deck/discard handling, valid-state invariants).

- **Testing — browser smoke test:** At least one targeted browser test verifies the panel opens from the Settings debug section and a card can be chosen by mouse.

- **Build validation:** `npm run build` succeeds and the production bundle does not contain the debug card-picker code (tree-shake verified).

- **Documentation:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` includes a note about the new cheat tool under Main Street Debug Tools; all related documentation is updated.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing dev-mode debug framework: `isDevMode()` / `DebugToolsRegistry.DebugToolsEntry` (`src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts`), `SettingsPanel` `debugTools` rendering, and `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` default debug-tools wiring — follow the pattern of `SessionExportTool`, `StateInspectorOverlay`, `GameEventLogOverlay`, `AiDecisionOverlay`. Gate the tool via `import.meta.env.DEV` so it is tree-shaken from production bundles.
- **Absolute no-no:** No debug/release transition bugs — the feature must be completely absent in production (no UI, no reachable code path, no bundle bloat). No arbitrary code execution or file-system access from the picker.
- Market model is single-row, exactly `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS` (3) cards (`MainStreetCards.ts`); replacement targets `state.market.cards` (Main Street state) and must go through the existing renderer (`MainStreetRenderer`) and animation/layout paths rather than bypassing them.
- Card pool is the CSV-backed template registry (`MainStreetCards.ts` `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES` / `get*Templates()` / `getCsvRows()`); the picker must handle runtime CSV reload (`loadTemplatesFromCsv`) and tier-gated pools (unlocked-card filtering) without duplicating template data inline.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetCards.ts` defines all five families, CSV-backed templates (`getBusinessTemplates()` etc.), `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS = 3`, and `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`; `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetState.ts` own `state.market.cards` and market lifecycle (refill/cycle/refresh).
- Dev-mode Debug Tools framework exists (`src/ui/debug/`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`) with `isDevMode()`, `DebugToolsEntry`, and default tools (`SessionExport`, `StateInspector`, `GameEventLog`, `AiDecisionViewer`); production gating via `import.meta.env.DEV` is established.
- No existing mechanism forces an arbitrary card into the market — market contents are derived from the seeded deck + cycling; reproducing specific-card scenarios requires seed manipulation or save hacking.

## Desired Change

- Register a new `DebugToolsEntry` (e.g. `createMarketCardCheatTool`) that opens a card picker overlay/window: grouped by family/type, with a type filter and a partial-title text filter, navigable by mouse and keyboard (arrow keys + Enter).
- On confirm, replace a uniformly-random entry of `state.market.cards` with a freshly-instantiated card from the chosen template (unique instance `id`), return the displaced card to its family discard/deck per existing lifecycle, and re-render the market row (reuse `MainStreetRenderer` / `MainStreetScene` refresh path). Ensure save/load, undo/redo, and transcript invariants remain intact.
- Wire the tool into the default debug-tools set (or Main-Street-specific override of `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`) and document it.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts` — `isDevMode()` + `DebugToolsEntry` interface; extended with the new entry factory.
- `src/ui/debug/index.ts` — Barrel re-export; add the new tool factory.
- `src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — `initSettingsPanel` default `debugTools` wiring; register the new tool (globally or via Main Street scene override).
- `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` — Debug Tools section rendering (consumes `debugTools`); no structural change expected, but verify scroll/selection interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Card pool source of truth: `MARKET_TOTAL_SLOTS`, `CARD_TEMPLATE_NAMES`, `getBusinessTemplates()` / `getCommunitySpaceTemplates()` / `getEventTemplates()` / `getUpgradeTemplates()` / `getStaffCardTemplates()`, `getCsvRows()` / `loadTemplatesFromCsv` / tier helpers; add any small helpers for "instantiate a fresh card from a template id" if not already centralized.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `state.market.cards` shape and deck/discard families (move displaced card to correct pile).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Market lifecycle (refill/cycle/discard routing) — where to slot the cheat's state mutation so it obeys the same invariants.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Scene wiring: renderer ownership, debug-tools override, overlay dismissal, keyboard focus management for the picker.
- `src/ui/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` (new) — Overlay/window implementation: grouped list, type filter, title substring filter, arrow-key + Enter + mouse selection, confirm → engine call, cancel/dismiss.

## Related Work

- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Developer workflow, testing, and Main Street local development; will need a note about the new debug cheat.
  - `src/ui/debug/DebugToolsRegistry.ts`, `src/ui/debug/StateInspectorOverlay.ts`, `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`, `src/ui/debug/AiDecisionOverlay.ts` — Canonical patterns for overlay-based debug tools registered as `DebugToolsEntry`.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - Detect when running in developer mode and provide debug tools (CG-0MQZYFG3C0063DN3) — Epic that created the Debug Tools framework; this item extends it.
  - Dev mode detection & Debug section framework (CG-0MS217X1F0089SAM) — Created `isDevMode()` / `SettingsPanel` debug section.
  - Session export in Debug section (CG-0MS1QC3RR004J4Y5), Game Event Log debug tool (CG-0MS1QC3KR004C7UQ), and siblings — Prior art for adding entries to the debug section.
  - Minimal Card System & Market (CG-0MM7IA8UB0BOEXZ5), Single-row market UI & input flows (CG-0MSW6ITE50095JJ4), MarketOfferEngine Extraction (CG-0MPWZ5RYR005VX1F) — Market implementation history.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The card pool is exactly the runtime template registry in `MainStreetCards.ts` (CSV-backed, `get*Templates()`); if the pool is expected to include only unlocked/tier-available cards, the picker should consult the current unlock state rather than the full catalog — confirm desired scope during implementation.
- **Risk — debug code leaks into production:** Mitigate by gating factory creation/import behind `import.meta.env.DEV` in `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel` and verifying the production bundle does not contain picker code (bundle inspection / smoke test).
- **Risk — state corruption (duplicate ids, discard/deck inconsistency):** Mitigate by instantiating the replacement via a dedicated helper that clones the template with a unique instance `id` (e.g. `${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and by routing the displaced card through the existing discard path per family.
- **Risk — accessibility / focus management:** Arrow-key + Enter navigation and focus trapping inside the overlay must work alongside `SettingsPanel` and existing HUD overlays — follow patterns in `StateInspectorOverlay` / `GameEventLogOverlay` for scroll, mask, and dismiss handling.
- **Risk — scope creep (deck editors, multi-card injection, staff-skill reseed):** Treat richer cheats (add-to-deck, reseed skills, inject multiple cards) as follow-up work items rather than extending this item — this item replaces a single random market card only.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extra cheat concepts surfaced during planning (e.g. deck/discard editors, tier override, skill reseed) should be filed as separate `discovered-from:CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5` work items.

## Effort & Risk (to be filled by /skill:effort-and-risk)

*Filled by `orchestrate_estimate.py` after intake.*

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

# Intake Brief — Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6)

## Problem statement

Coins and reputation currently use fractional decimals (e.g. `2.3`, `0.05`) across the CSV and engine. Floating point accumulation and mixed `toFixed(1/2/3)` display makes values hard to reason about and compare. The codebase should operate entirely on whole numbers.

## Users

- **Game designer / balancer** — wants to read and tune card values as integers without mental decimal conversion; needs CSV to be the single source of truth.
- **Player** — sees clean integer coin/reputation values in HUD, tooltips, card text, and logs without spurious decimals like `5.000` or `2.30`.

### User stories

- As a designer, I can open `card-data.csv` and see every coin/reputation-relevant field as an integer so that I can balance without chasing floating-point rounding errors.
- As a player, I see coins and reputation as whole numbers everywhere in the UI so that feedback is immediate and consistent.
- As a developer, any coin/reputation calculation yields an integer (rounded to nearest) so that game state never accumulates fractional drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV integer migration** — Every coin/reputation-relevant column in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (`cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `synergyCoinBonus`, `synergyRepBonus`, `ongoingCost`, `incomeBonus`, `reputationBonus`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `synergyRangeBonus`, plus staff/effect multipliers where they represent coin/rep amounts) is multiplied by 100 and rounded to the nearest integer (`Math.round`). No fractional values remain in those columns; synergy *rates* that are true percentages (0–1 range) are called out explicitly if kept as decimals, otherwise also scaled.
2. **No decimal formatting in UI** — All `toFixed(1/2/3)` and `formatCurrency` decimal paths for coins/reputation are removed or switched to integer rendering: HUD bar (`MainStreetRenderer`, `MainStreetOverlayContent`), tooltips (`MainStreetHudTooltips`), card SVGs (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator`), activity logs (`MainStreetAdjacency`, `MainStreetState`), and `src/core-engine/I18n.ts` `formatCurrency` behavior for these fields. Spot-check: HUD shows `Coins: 123` not `Coins: 123.00`.
3. **Calculations round to nearest integer** — Every coin/reputation arithmetic path rounds its result to the nearest integer (e.g. synergy product `baseIncome * synergyRate * adjacency`, `applyReputationMultiplier`, `applyReputationMultiplier`, event deltas, ongoing-cost deductions, sell/premium pricing, income multiplier effects) using `Math.round` semantics. Document the rounding boundary (applied per-card/per-event/per-turn vs. single final aggregation) in a code comment at the central helper(s).
4. **Tests and balance artifacts updated** — All affected unit/browser tests are updated to expect integer values and pass; any checked-in balance snapshots or CSV-derived artifacts (e.g. card SVGs, checksums) are regenerated. Full project test suite passes.
5. **Documentation updated** — Code comments, `docs/` and `example-games/main-street/README.md` or `docs/main-street/*` references that describe decimal precision (e.g. "3dp", "to 2 decimal places") are revised to describe integer semantics. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`** — CSV migration is `value * 100 → Math.round`; keep integer costs already correct (e.g. `3 → 300`); do not hand-tweak individual values outside that rule unless a follow-up balance pass is explicitly scoped.
- **No floating-point drift** — After this change `state.resourceBank.coins` and `state.resourceBank.reputation` must remain integers through normal play; avoid reintroducing fractional intermediates without rounding.
- **Backwards-compatibility note** — Saved games / transcripts that contain decimal coin/rep values will be incompatible; call out migration or intentional breakage in the PR description; no silent coercion that masks data loss.
- **Scope guard** — Synergy *rates* vs. amounts: if any `synergyCoinBonus`/`synergyRepBonus` field is defined as a true rate (e.g. `0.5 = 50%`) rather than an amount, confirm its intended semantics before scaling; record the decision in the work item.
- **Minimal churn** — Touch only coin/reputation paths; unrelated numeric systems (e.g. `multiplier` for income-multiplier events like `0.8`, turn counters) are out of scope unless they feed coin/rep calculations.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` contains fractional coin/rep fields (`baseIncome 2.3`, `reputationPerTurn 0.05`, `ongoingCost 0.75`, `coinDelta -2` alongside fractional event deltas, etc.).
- UI formats with `toFixed(2)` (HUD), `toFixed(3)` (logs/adjacency), `toFixed(1)` (reputation/synergy rate labels), and `formatCurrency` which currently renders whatever number is passed.
- Engine accumulates floats in `resourceBank`, `EconomyLedger`, and per-turn income/reputation resolution (`MainStreetEngine`, `MainStreetAdjacency`, `MainStreetMarket`, `MainStreetDifficulty`).
- Prior work (CG-0MRER3RE300418SG, CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0) addressed rounding/display in isolation; this item unifies on integers.

## Desired change

- Migrate all coin/reputation CSV values to integers (`Math.round(value * 100)`), strip decimal formatting from every UI surface, and make every coin/reputation calculation round to the nearest integer so the entire economy is integer-only.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Scale all coin/rep columns ×100 and round.
- `src/core-engine/I18n.ts` — Adjust `formatCurrency` / currency rendering to integer display for migrated fields.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Remove `toFixed(2)` HUD formatting; render integer coins/rep.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Remove `toFixed(2)` game-over overlay.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — Remove `toFixed(3)`/`toFixed(1)` coin/rep displays.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Integer cost/reputation rendering; `toFixed(1)` helper removal.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — Integer synergy math and log formatting (`toFixed(3)`).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `describeEventEffects` integer formatting.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `applyReputationMultiplier` / `reputationCoinMultiplier` rounding.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Ongoing-cost, event, favour, bankruptcy log (`toFixed(3)`) and any coin/rep arithmetic.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Sell value, premium cost, hire/upgrade logs and arithmetic.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — CSV parsing / type contracts for migrated columns.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Tooltip/card text formatters (rate vs amount handling).
- `tests/main-street/**` — Update expectations from fractional to integer values.

## Related work

- **Potentially related docs**
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — canonical card/effect data; source of the decimal values.
  - `src/core-engine/I18n.ts` — `formatCurrency` and currency symbol handling.
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` / `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — describe card values and balance methodology (check for decimal-precision language).
  - `example-games/main-street/README.md` — documents CSV as source of truth.

- **Potentially related work items**
  - `Show HUD bar money and reputation to 2 decimal places (CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0)` — completed; established `toFixed(2)` HUD behavior now being removed.
  - `Income rounding error: fractional baseIncome lost via Math.floor in applyReputationMultiplier (CG-0MRER3RE300418SG)` — completed; fixed rounding loss that this integer migration supersedes.
  - `Tooltips on businesses are confusing (CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ)` — completed; touched tooltip coin/rep formatting (`formatCurrency` / integer conventions).
  - `When selling a businesses in Main Street sale price should reflect value of business (CG-0MT5XO7DI0066QCT)` — completed; sell-value formula (`Math.ceil`/`Math.floor`) that must now operate on integer inputs.
  - Search `wl search "coins reputation integer"` surfaced 5 items; worktree scans confirm decimal patterns cluster in Main Street engine/scenes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: rate vs. amount ambiguity** — `synergyCoinBonus`/`synergyRepBonus` could be rates (e.g. `0.5 = 50%`) not amounts; blindly ×100 would inflate them 100×. Mitigation: verify semantics before migration (check `MainStreetAdjacency`/`MainStreetCards` usage); treat true rates as exempt and document.
- **Risk: missed arithmetic paths** — Coin/rep math is spread across Engine/Market/Adjacency/Difficulty/Formatting; a missed `*` or division could reintroduce floats. Mitigation: grep for `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`/`baseIncome`/`ongoingCost`/`applyReputationMultiplier` and add a central `roundInt` helper.
- **Risk: save/transcript incompatibility** — Integer migration breaks load of old saves/transcripts with fractional values. Mitigation: explicitly version or invalidate old saves; document in release notes.
- **Risk: balance shift** — ×100 with `Math.round` changes effective economy by two orders of magnitude; tunings that felt small before (0.05 rep) become 5. Mitigation: this is intentional per brief; do not rebalance in this item — file a separate balance-pass child if needed.
- **Risk: scope creep (rebalance)** — Temptation to retune costs/income while migrating. Mitigation: strictly apply `×100 + round`; any hand-tuned balance changes go to a linked follow-up work item.
- **Assumption:** All coin/reputation fields should be integers; no field intentionally needs sub-coin granularity after migration.
- **Assumption:** `formatCurrency` should render integer amounts without decimals after this change (e.g. `€300` not `€3.00`); locale symbol handling stays as-is.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked during this intake. The work item description provided explicit migration rules (CSV ×100 + round, strip decimal formatting, round calculations to nearest integer) and was sufficient to draft a clear brief without an interview round.

- Q: (not asked) — Seed context was sufficient; no producer interview was conducted. Source: `wl show CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 --json` description.
- Research: `wl search "coins reputation integer"` (5 hits) + repo grep for `toFixed`/`formatCurrency`/`coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`/`baseIncome`/`ongoingCost` confirmed decimal usage clusters in `example-games/main-street/` scenes/engine and `src/core-engine/I18n.ts`; `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` sampled directly — fractional fields confirmed (file read). Related work items CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0, CG-0MRER3RE300418SG, CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ, CG-0MT5XO7DI0066QCT summarized from FTS snippets; full descriptions not re-fetched (low signal for AC definition).

# Do not show new market cards until turn has ended

## Problem statement

When the player clicks "End Turn", the market cards are cycled (old cards discarded, new cards dealt from deck) **immediately** inside `processEndOfTurn()`, before income calculation, incident resolution, and the 800ms delay. This leaves the player staring at newly dealt market cards while income/incident animations and log updates play out — a jarring disconnect where the player is looking at the next day's market before their current turn has finished resolving.

## Users

- **User story:** As a Main Street player, I want the market to stay unchanged during my turn's end-of-turn resolution (income, incidents, notifications) so I can see the full financial summary of the turn I just played.
- **User story:** As a player, I want the new market cards to appear only when the next day begins, giving me a clean visual transition between turns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Clicking "End Turn" no longer cycles the market cards. The old market cards remain visible during income calculation, incident resolution, and the income-feedback display.
- **AC2:** The market cards are cycled and refilled at the **start** of the next day (inside `startDayPhase()` / `executeDayStart()`), so the player sees the new market alongside the "Day N" transition banner.
- **AC3:** All existing unit tests pass, including `MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` and `staff-general-market-state.test.ts`. No regression in market cycling correctness.
- **AC4:** Tutorial gameplay is unaffected — scenario-placed market cards are still preserved across the day boundary as before.
- **AC5:** Competitive mode (multi-player) is unaffected — the same market-cycling behavior applies at the correct point in the closing phases.

## Constraints

- The `cycleMarketCards()` function itself is **not changed** — only its call site moves.
- The tutorial's `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` flag and related guard code can be **removed** since cycling no longer happens during end-of-turn processing.
- The market must still be refilled at day start — only the timing of the cycle changes (from end of old turn → start of new turn).

## Existing state

Market cards are cycled at the beginning of `processEndOfTurn()` in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
- **Line ~1430-1431** (single-player): `if (!state.skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn) { cycleMarketCards(state); }`
- **Line ~1212** (competitive): `if (!state.skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn) cycleMarketCards(state);`

Then income, incidents, and notifications play — the player sees the new cards during this wait.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** the `cycleMarketCards(state)` call from `processEndOfTurn()` (line ~1430-1431) and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` (line ~1212).
2. **Add** a `cycleMarketCards(state)` call in `executeDayStart()` right after the `refillMarket(state)` call (after line ~1264 in `MainStreetEngine.ts`). This ensures cycling happens at the start of each new day.
3. **Remove** the `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` state field, its guard in `processEndOfTurn()`, and its setting/clearing in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`.
4. The `executeCompetitiveDay` path (line ~1334) that calls `refillMarket` in `executeDayStart` already has a `skipMarketRefill` parameter — the new `cycleMarketCards` call should follow the same skip logic (skip on checkpoint resume).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Move `cycleMarketCards` from `processEndOfTurn()` and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` to `executeDayStart()`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Remove `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` guard in `endTurn()`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Remove `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` state field (~line 377)
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetMarketCycling.test.ts` — Verify tests still pass (they call `cycleMarketCards` directly, so no change needed)
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Review if any scenario assumptions about market timing need updating

## Related work

- CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 — Add visible game activity log to Main Street UI (income/incident logging)
- CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ — Main Street log should show total effects (per-turn net summary)
- CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P — Tutorial: two-turn plan-ahead flow (uses `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` to preserve scenario cards)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The tutorial's `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` flag also suppresses cycling — removing it could cause scenario cards to be lost on end-turn. **Mitigation:** The cycle now happens in `startDayPhase()` which the tutorial already goes through, so scenario cards should still be preserved by `refillMarket()`'s top-up semantics (visible cards are preserved, only missing slots are drawn).
- **Assumption:** The `refillMarket()` top-up semantics (preserve visible cards, only draw into empty slots) correctly preserve scenario cards. If not, the scenario system may need an additional guard in `executeDayStart()`.
- **Scope creep:** This change only affects the timing of market cycling. No changes to market composition, card deal animations, or income calculation logic.
- **Assumption:** Competitive mode only calls `processEndOfTurn()` / `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases()` from `executeCompetitiveDay()`, which in turn calls `executeDayStart()` for the next day — the new cycle location applies uniformly.

# Intake Brief: Grand Opening card can only be played in the same turn as a business is opened (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**

> Restrict Grand Opening Sale (`evt-grand-opening`) so it can only be played from hand during a turn in which a business has been placed onto the street grid; all other play timing remains unchanged.

## Problem Statement

The Grand Opening Sale Investment event (`evt-grand-opening`) can currently be played on any turn it is held, which dilutes its thematic tie to opening a new business. The desired mechanic is a same-turn combo: the event should only be playable in the turn a business is placed onto the street, rewarding coordinated play.

## Users

- **Player:** Wants the Grand Opening card to feel like a celebration of a new opening, with clear feedback about when it can be used.
  - *"As a player, I want to play Grand Opening Sale only on a turn where I opened a business, so the reward feels earned and the timing is meaningful."*
- **Game Designer / Balancer:** Needs the restriction enforced consistently across all placement paths and visible to AI/balance tooling.
  - *"As a designer, I want Grand Opening's play window enforced in the engine's legality layer so balance assumptions about its frequency hold."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Turn-gated play for Grand Opening:** `evt-grand-opening` can be played from hand (`play-event-from-hand` / `play-event`) only when a business has been placed onto the street during the current turn (Day). Attempts to play it in a turn with no placement are rejected as illegal (legality check returns `legal: false` with a clear reason; UI shows illegal-move shake/feedback and no state mutation).
2. **All placement paths arm the gate:** The "business placed this turn" flag is set by every street-placement path — `playBusinessFromHand`, `purchaseBusiness` (direct buy-and-place via market), and `buy-and-place` composite — and is checked by the Grand Opening legality. Verified by unit coverage for each path (same-turn placement → Grand Opening playable; no placement → blocked).
3. **Gate lifecycle:** The flag resets at `DayStart` (new day) and does not carry over; placing multiple businesses in one turn keeps the gate open for that turn only. Holding Grand Opening across turns without a placement keeps it unplayable until a new placement occurs.
4. **No regression for other events:** All other Investment events (e.g. Local Festival, free Community Garden, etc.) remain playable any turn they are held and affordable, subject only to existing action/coin/hand rules. Existing event tests and tutorial flows continue to pass.
5. **Testing & validation:** Unit tests cover the gating (allowed vs blocked cases, reset on new day, each placement path, and coin/action edge cases); at least one browser/interaction check confirms illegal-play feedback; `npm run build` succeeds.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **CSV is source of truth unchanged:** No schema change to `card-data.csv`; `evt-grand-opening` row stays as `SpecificSynergy/Commerce` with existing cost/deltas. Gating is engine logic, not data.
- **Legality-layer enforcement:** The restriction must live in the engine's legality helpers (`canPlayEvent` / `playEventFromHand` and the `executeAction` play-event path), not only in the scene/UI, so headless, AI, and replay paths respect it.
- **Deterministic per turn:** Same seed + same action sequence produces the same allowed/blocked outcome; no extra RNG consumed for the gate.
- **AI respects the gate:** AI strategy skips `evt-grand-opening` when the turn gate is not satisfied.
- **Backwards-compatible save shape:** Any new state field (e.g. `businessPlacedThisTurn` / `placedBusinessIdsThisTurn`) must have a safe default and migration for old saves.

## Existing State

- **Event model:** Investment events are moved to hand for free (`moveToHand` / `purchaseEvent` with cost 0) and played from hand via `playEventFromHand` / `playEventCommand`, paying `card.cost` at play time and resolving `SpecificSynergy` effects (see `MainStreetMarket.playEventFromHand`, `MainStreetEngine.executeAction` play-event cases).
- **Current legality for events:** `canPlayEvent` checks hand index, family `event`, trigger `Investment`, same-day composite action waiver, `actionsRemaining`, and `coins`; no placement check. `canPurchaseEvent` is hand-capacity only. `resolveEvent` for `SpecificSynergy` counts matching businesses on the grid.
- **Placement paths:** Businesses/community-spaces reach the grid via `purchaseBusiness`, `playBusinessFromHand` (cost-at-play), and `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (+50% premium drag path). Turn-scoped flags already exist for same-day composites (`justMovedHandCardId`, `justMovedEventCardId`, `justMovedUpgradeCardId`); business placement has no turn-scoped "placed this turn" flag yet.
- **Card identity:** `evt-grand-opening` ("Grand Opening Sale", cost 3, `SpecificSynergy/Commerce`, `coinDelta 4.5`) is an Investment-trigger event; other Investment events share the same family/trigger but should not be gated.

## Desired Change

### 1. Turn-scoped placement flag

- Add a per-turn flag to `MainStreetState` (e.g. `businessPlacedThisTurn: boolean` or `businessPlacedTurn: number | null`), initialized to `false`/`null`, set to `true` whenever a business or community-space card is successfully placed onto `streetGrid` (all three placement paths), and reset to `false` in `executeDayStart` / `executeCompetitiveDayStart` (DayStart). Competitive mode shares the same day, so the flag is shared for the day. Persist with a safe default and backfill in `deserialize`/`migrate`.

### 2. Gate Grand Opening on the flag

- In `canPlayEvent` (and the underlying `playEventFromHand` validation) and in `executeAction`'s `play-event` / `play-event-from-hand` branches, when the target card id is `evt-grand-opening` (or name "Grand Opening Sale"), require `businessPlacedThisTurn === true`; otherwise return `legal: false` with a message like "Grand Opening Sale can only be played on a turn where you opened a business." `purchaseEvent` (move to hand) stays ungated — the card can be acquired any turn, only playing is gated.

- Surface illegal-play feedback via the existing `shakeIllegalMove` / instruction-text path when the scene attempts the gated play outside the window.

### 3. AI and docs

- Update `MainStreetAiStrategy` scoring/filtering so the AI does not select `evt-grand-opening` when the gate is closed.
- Update `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` entry for `evt-grand-opening` (effect/timing note), `example-games/main-street/README.md` or card-data comments, and the engine's `AGENTS.md` / `docs/DEVELOPER.md` if the turn-gate pattern is described.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Add `businessPlacedThisTurn` (or equivalent) to `MainStreetState`, initialize in `createInitialState`/`createMainStreetState`, reset on DayStart, handle save/load migration.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Gate `canPlayEvent` / `playEventFromHand` for `evt-grand-opening` on the new flag; set the flag in `purchaseBusiness`, `playBusinessFromHand`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (or centralize in the callers).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Reset flag in `executeDayStart` / `executeCompetitiveDayStart`; enforce gate in `executeAction` play-event branches if not already covered by market legality; wire `consumeAction` ordering.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Filter/score `evt-grand-opening` against the gate in legal-action selection.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Surface illegal-play feedback for the gated case (if not already via engine error path).
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Document new timing restriction for Grand Opening Sale.
- `tests/main-street/**` — New/updated unit coverage for the gate (allowed vs blocked, reset, each placement path); browser smoke for shake/feedback.

## Related work

- **Market / hand economy (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2)** [completed]: Unified single-row market, move-to-hand is free, play-from-hand pays cost-at-play — the layer this gate builds on. `MainStreetMarket.moveToHand` / `playBusinessFromHand` / `playEventFromHand`.
- **Event cost-at-play (CG-0MT5W1V4D007NN8Q)** [completed]: Investment events moved to hand free, cost paid on play — establishes the `justMovedEventCardId` / `canPlayEvent` pattern the gate will extend.
- **Business placement premium (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN)** [completed]: Same-day composite vs plan-ahead pricing for `playBusinessFromHand` / `buy-and-place` — the placement paths that must arm the gate.
- **Tutorial T7: Replace Grand Opening with Local Festival (CG-0MR481920006RAO5)** [completed]: Tutorial no longer hinges on `evt-grand-opening` in the investments row; reduces blast radius for this change.
- **Upgrade buy-and-place premium (CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP)** [in progress/open]: Parallel +50% premium pattern for upgrades — not gated, but shares placement plumbing.
- **Core engine: charge an action for event move/play (CG-0MTH5CA9R0023PKU)** [open]: Action-economy work that touches `canPlayEvent` / `executeAction` event paths; coordinate to avoid double-charging the gated play.

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Scope creep — card-specific rule in generic event plumbing:** Adding a per-card exception to generic event legality could invite more card-specific branches. Mitigation: isolate the check to `card.id === 'evt-grand-opening'` (or a `requiresBusinessPlacedThisTurn` flag on the card type if preferred) with a single enforcement point; record further card-specific timing ideas as separate work items.
- **Missed placement path:** If any business-placement entry point is missed, the gate appears flaky. Mitigation: enumerate and test all three paths (`purchaseBusiness`, `playBusinessFromHand`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`) plus competitive shared-day.
- **Save compatibility:** Old saves lacking the new flag must not break. Mitigation: default `false` and backfill in deserialization.
- **AI / Monte Carlo drift:** Gating reduces Grand Opening frequency, shifting economy balance. Mitigation: AI respects the gate; Monte Carlo guardrails reviewed if scores shift materially.

### Assumptions

- The restriction applies only to **playing** `evt-grand-opening` from hand, not to acquiring it (moving to hand remains free any turn). If the producer intends acquisition to also be gated, the brief will be amended.
- "Business is opened" means a **business or community-space** card placed onto `streetGrid` this turn (both families occupy grid slots). If only `business` family should count, the implementation will narrow the flag to `card.family === 'business'`.
- The gate is **turn-scoped** (resets at `DayStart`), not phase-scoped; multiple placements in one turn keep it open for that turn.
- No change to `evt-grand-opening`'s CSV cost, synergy target, or deltas; only play legality changes.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. **Q: Does "business is opened" include community-space cards (which also occupy the street grid) or only `family === 'business'`?**
   - A: Assumed to include both `business` and `community-space` placements (they share the same `streetGrid` placement plumbing). Source: assumption for intake; to be confirmed by producer. If the producer wants business-only, narrow the flag to `card.family === 'business'`. Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — confirm family scope.

2. **Q: Should acquiring Grand Opening to hand also be gated, or only playing it?**
   - A: Assumed only **playing** is gated; `moveToHand`/`purchaseEvent` for `evt-grand-opening` stays free any turn. Source: assumption for intake; aligns with existing "move free, pay on play" model (CG-0MT5W1V4D007NN8Q). Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — confirm acquisition vs play scope.

3. **Q: Is the gate per-turn (Day) or per-phase? Does placing multiple businesses extend the window?**
   - A: Assumed per-turn (Day), reset at `DayStart`; multiple placements keep the gate open for that turn only. Source: assumption based on issue title "same turn." Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — confirm reset boundary.

4. **Q: Should the gate apply to the direct buy-and-place drag path that places a business and could then play Grand Opening in the same MarketPhase?**
   - A: Assumed yes — any successful `streetGrid` placement arms the gate for the remainder of that turn's `MarketPhase`, so a drag-placed business followed by Grand Opening in the same phase is legal. Source: assumption; to be confirmed. Status: **OPEN QUESTION**.

# Market Card Cheat Tool (CG-0MTINKHUT009KHK5)

Create `createMarketCardCheatTool()` — a new `DebugToolsEntry` that opens a card-picker overlay.

## Summary

On confirm, replaces a uniformly-random market slot with a fresh instance of the selected card template, returning the displaced card to its family's discard pile.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New `MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` implements `DebugToolsEntry` with label "Market Card Cheat" and description "Replace a random market card with any card from the pool".
- The tool is registered in Main Street's debug tools (via `MainStreetScene` override of `debugTools` passed to `initSettingsPanel()`), appearing in the Settings panel Debug Tools section.
- The card picker groups all 5 families (Business, Community Space, Event, Upgrade, Staff) with type filter checkboxes and a case-insensitive partial-title text search; filters compose (type ∩ text).
- Keyboard navigation: arrow keys move selection focus through the list, Enter confirms; mouse click selects and confirms.
- On confirm: a random slot from `state.market.cards` (among 3) is replaced with a shallow-copied card instance (unique id like `${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`), the displaced card goes to its family's discard pile, and the market row re-renders via existing renderer path.
- Dev-mode gated: factory is only called when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true; absent from production builds.

## Implementation Notes

- Follow the pattern of `StateInspectorOverlay.ts`: create a scrollable overlay dialog using `createOverlayDialog`, with DOM input for text search and Phaser text objects for the card list.
- The replacement helper should go in `MainStreetMarket.ts` (or `MainStreetEngine.ts`): a function like `cheatReplaceMarketCard(state, chosenTemplateId)` that:
  - Picks a random index from `state.market.cards` (uniform over current slots)
  - Creates a shallow copy of the template with a unique id
  - Pushes the displaced card to the appropriate family's discard pile
  - Returns the new card
- Wire into `MainStreetScene` by overriding `debugTools` in `initSettingsPanel()`:
  ```ts
  protected initSettingsPanel(): void {
    const debugTools: DebugToolsEntry[] = import.meta.env.DEV ? [
      ...defaultDebugTools,
      createMarketCardCheatTool(),
    ] : [];
    super.initSettingsPanel(undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, debugTools);
  }
  ```

## Key Files:
- `src/ui/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts`
- `src/ui/debug/index.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts`

# Harden vite-transcript-plugin-regression dev-server smoke against ENOSPC (watch limit)

**Priority: Critical** | **Type: Bug** | **Discovered from: CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC (ENOSPC false-positive at HEAD a8fb638d)**

## Problem

`tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` — the dev-server smoke suite that guards the transcript-persist OOM regression (CG-0MSXL0A25 / CG-0MSXNMDZ6) — triggered an ENOSPC (errno -28, syscall watch) infrastructure failure during the full-suite run at HEAD a8fb638d. 328/329 files passed, 6020/6030 tests passed; the single failure was `NodeFsHandler._watchWithNodeFs` in Vite's chokidar watcher, not an assertion failure.

The test boots an in-process Vite dev server with `root: project root` and `configFile: vite.config.ts`. That server inherits the repo watcher which, combined with 15–19 active `.worklog/worktrees/` checkouts (each with node_modules/assets/layouts), exceeds the default `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` (typically 8192). The watch path in the failure was inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-CG-0MRYZ.../public/assets/cards/lost-cities`) — the production watcher is not supposed to watch worktrees, but the test server's watcher did.

This is a **valuable regression guard** (it asserts the bounded-body contract and the watcher-ignore for the transcript output tree, AC1/AC2/AC4 deterministic proxies for the OOM). Deleting it would re-open the OOM vector. The fix is to harden, not remove.

## Root Cause

- Vite dev server started in the test watches the project root (required for `getWatched()` assertion) but does not exclude `.worklog/worktrees/**` from its watcher. Under many concurrent worktrees the inotify budget is exhausted even before the suite finishes.
- `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` already contains `**/data/**` for the transcript output tree, but not worktrees.
- No fallback: ENOSPC surfaces as a serialized error that fails the file, triaged as a real test failure (CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **ENOSPC no longer fails the suite**: the dev-server smoke either (a) configures the server watcher to ignore `.worklog/**` / `.worklog/worktrees/**` (e.g. `server.watch.ignored` or `watcher.ignored`), or (b) handles ENOSPC gracefully (skip/diagnostic, not hard fail) so the guard suite does not become a flaky gate under many worktrees. Re-run `npm --silent test` with 10+ worktrees present and verify 329/329 files pass or the guard degrades to a clear skip.
2. **Guard semantics preserved**: the existing assertions remain — bounded body cap (DEFAULT_MAX_BODY_BYTES bound, 413 over cap, 200 for realistic transcript, watch-ignore for transcript tree, POST does not add tmpDir to watcher, 413 on live server). No weakening of the OOM regression coverage.
3. **Worktree hygiene documented or enforced**: either the watcher ignore covers worktrees, or a beforeAll guard checks `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and emits an actionable diagnostic ("increase max_user_watches to 524288 or prune worktrees"), so CI/local operators get a fix, not a mystery ENOSPC.
4. **Full suite green**: `npm --silent test` exits 0 at the fix commit; audit of this item shows 0 watch-related flakes under normal worktree load. Previous false-positive triage CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC can be closed as resolved by this hardening.

## Key Files

- `tests/vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts:66-120` — dev-server smoke (beforeAll createServer, server.watcher.getWatched, POST loop)
- `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS, transcriptPersistPlugin
- `vite.config.ts` — Vitest watcher / server.watch config

## Links

- False-positive triage (to close on fix): CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC
- OOM original: CG-0MSXL0A25009WZVK, profiling: CG-0MSXNMDZ6004RA6I
- Related speed-profile parent (context): CG-0MSZ4TN5Z001JADX

# Intake Brief — End-of-turn VFX/SFX scaled to x100 economy — 1 visual/SFX per 100 coins (CG-0MTK2JHXD004KNQI)

## Problem statement

After the integer-economy migration (`×100`: 1 old coin = 100 new coins, CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) end-of-turn income awards ~100× more integer coins but the phased income animation (`MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases`) and legacy `animateIncomeCollection` still create **1 visual coin icon + 1 `COIN_POP` SFX per 1 integer coin**. A modest old income of 3 coins now spawns ~300 icons and ~300 SFX, creating visual clutter, audio spam, and performance pressure. Visual/SFX density should scale with the economy: **1 coin icon + 1 SFX per 100 integer coins** (i.e. per 1 old coin).

## Users

- **Player** — ends a turn and watches income collection. Wants income feedback that is readable and pleasant: a handful of coins flying and a few pops that convey magnitude, not a flood of hundreds of coins/sounds.
- **Developer / balancer** — tunes `card-data.csv` integer values (`baseIncome`, buffs, event deltas) and expects the animation layer to stay proportional without manual VFX tweaks per balance change.

### User stories

- As a player, when I end a turn that earns 300 coins (≈3 old coins), I see ~3 coins animate (not 300) and hear ~3 pops, so the feedback feels like it did before the `×100` change.
- As a player, when I earn 0 coins that turn, I see no coins fly and hear no coin pops (existing no-op path, unchanged).
- As a developer, changing a card's `baseIncome` from 100 to 250 integer coins predictably changes that phase's visuals from ~1 to ~3 icons without code changes to the animator.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Visual scaling (phased income)** — Every income-phase visual that creates coin icons (`countOutCoins` for base, `flyCoinsIn`/`flyCoinsOut` for synergy/reputation/event/upcoming, and `collectIncomeGrids` grid-to-HUD sweep) creates **1 icon per 100 integer coins**. Concretely, icon count per phase amount `a` is `Math.round(Math.max(0, a) / 100)` (or equivalent ceiling/clamp documented in code), capped to what `packCoins` can pack. Example: `baseIncome` 230 → 2 icons; 50 → 1 icon (small positive amounts remain visible); 0 → 0 icons. The change applies to all paths inside `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomePhases` and the grid handles it creates via `coin-grid.ts` (`splitCoins`/`packCoins`/`CoinGridHandle`). Legacy `animateIncomeCollection` (if still reachable) is either updated identically or documented as deprecated/unused.
2. **SFX scaling** — `COIN_POP` (`SFX_KEYS.COIN_POP` / `sfx-coin-pop`) fires **once per visual icon** (not per underlying integer coin). Total coin-pop SFX per income phase equals the visual icon count from AC1. Reputation pips, incident sting (`INCOME_NEGATIVE`/`INCOME_POSITIVE`), synergy chime, and reduced-motion silent paths are unchanged except for the reduced coin-pop count. Mute/volume via `SoundManager` continues to be honoured.
3. **Totals and labels remain truthful** — The final `+<total>` HUD pop, HUD numeric values, activity log deltas, and `creditedIncomeTotal` calculations continue to show the **true integer credited total** (e.g. `+300`), not the scaled icon count. Only the icon/SFX count is scaled. Phase labels, stagger timing (`INCOME_*_STAGGER_MS`), `incomeCollectionActive` lifecycle, and turn-flow non-blocking behaviour are unchanged.
4. **Edge cases and a11y preserved** — Zero-income turns still no-op (no icons, no SFX). Small incomes (<100) still produce at least 1 icon when >0 so feedback is not invisible (the chosen rounding/clamp is documented). Reduced-motion still suppresses flights but retains the single `+<total>` pop; headless/replay (`scene.replayMode`) still returns immediately with no rendering/audio; `packCoins` overflow handling (shrink/overlap) is not regressed by the smaller icon counts.
5. **Tests and docs updated** — Existing and new unit/browser tests cover the scaling (e.g. animator unit test: 230 → 2 icons/2 SFX, 0 → 0, 50 → 1; collect sweep: N remaining icons → N visuals, not N×100). Full project test suite passes with the new changes. Related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. `npm run build` succeeds. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No gameplay/economy change** — Only presentation (icon count, SFX count, pack layout) is affected. `applyIncome`, `resourceBank.coins`, event/reputation calculations, and transcript values must not change.
- **Economy is integer-only** — Inputs are integer coins; scaling is a pure presentation divisor (`/ 100` + rounding). No fractional coin state is reintroduced.
- **Single source of the divisor** — The `100` factor should be a named constant or derived from the economy scaling (not hard-coded literals scattered across call sites) so a future economy re-scale only touches one place.
- **Sound convention** — SFX keys remain `sfx-` prefixed via `SFX_KEYS.COIN_POP` / `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`; no game-scoped string literals. Playback stays through `SoundManager`/`moveGameObject` `sfx` params.
- **Performance** — End-of-turn choreography must remain non-blocking and not regress frame rate; the fix should reduce work (fewer icons/tweens/SFX), not add it.

## Existing state

- `×100` integer economy landed in CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6: CSV values `×100`, `reputationCoinDivisor` 80→8000, `coin-grid.ts` and animator switched to integer-only (`Math.round`, `splitCoins` half-coin always false), SVGs regenerated.
- Phased income animation (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTDE9H0C0061D51) accumulates income per card into on-card `CoinGrid` handles, then sweeps to the HUD. Each phase effect directly maps coin amount → icon count via `splitCoins(amount).fullCoins` and fires one `COIN_POP` per icon (`countOutCoins`, `flyCoinsIn`, `flyCoinsOut`, `collectIncomeGrids`, `revealInGrid`). After `×100`, `amount` is ~100× larger so icon/SFX counts are ~100× larger.
- `coin-grid.ts` `packCoins`/`CoinGridHandle.addCoins` already handles shrink/overlap when many icons are packed, but the UX intent is to show a readable handful, not hundreds.

## Desired change

- Introduce a presentation scaling divisor (e.g. `COINS_PER_VISUAL = 100` or `VISUAL_COIN_DIVISOR`) in `coin-grid.ts` or `MainStreetAnimator.ts` (single source; shared with tests) and apply it at the **icon-count decision** — i.e. visual icon count = `visualCount(amount)` where `visualCount = round(amount / 100)` clamped to `>=1` when `amount > 0` if that policy is chosen. Keep `packCoins` pure (it still packs `visualCount` icons).
- Update all phased-income icon-creation sites to use the scaled count for both the grid update (`addCoins`/`revealInGrid`) and the SFX firing cadence. `collectIncomeGrids` sweeps the already-scaled remaining icons (no second division).
- Keep `creditedIncomeTotal` and the final `+<total>` text on the true total; document the divisor and the rounding/clamp policy in a code comment at the helper.
- Optionally deprecate or align `animateIncomeCollection` (legacy income collection) to the same divisor if it is still called; otherwise note it as unused.
- Add/adjust unit tests for the presentation helper and a focused animator/browser smoke test for the choreography; update any existing income-animation tests that assert icon/SFX counts.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — Scale all income-phase icon/SFX sites (`countOutCoins`, `flyCoinsIn`, `flyCoinsOut`, `collectIncomeGrids`, `revealInGrid`, `creditedIncomeTotal` display vs. visual split) to 1 per 100; add `visualCount` helper + constant and document rounding/clamp.
- `example-games/main-street/coin-grid.ts` — Add `COINS_PER_VISUAL` / `visualCoinCount` helper (or `packCoins` presentation wrapper) as the single divisor source; keep `packCoins`/`splitCoins` integer-only; document the presentation scaling.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — No logic change expected; verify `animateIncomePhases` call site passes true totals (visual scaling is animator-internal).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — No change expected; note that `IncomeResult`/`SlotPhaseBreakdown` remain true totals.
- `tests/main-street/coin-grid.test.ts` (or new `tests/main-street/main-street-animator-vfx-scaling.test.ts` / `tests/main-street/income-animation.test.ts`) — Unit tests for the divisor helper and for the scaled icon/SFX counts; update existing income-animation tests if they assert raw counts.

## Related work

- `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — Integer economy ×100 (parent cause; `coin-grid.ts` and animator made integer-only; synergyCoinBonus rate 0.5 unchanged).
- `CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ` — Animated income with multiple phases (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collect) and `animateIncomePhases` choreography.
- `CG-0MTDE9H0C0061D51` — On-card coin grid component (`packCoins`, `createCoinGrid`).
- `CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE` — Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD) — predecessor to the phased system.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `example-games/main-street/README.md` if they describe coin visuals.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption: divisor is 100** — `×100` is the economy factor; 1 visual per 100 integer coins restores pre-×100 density exactly. If the producer wants a different density (e.g. 1 per 50 for more flair), the constant makes it trivial to retune.
- **Assumption: small amounts remain visible** — The brief proposes `max(1, round(a/100))` for `a > 0` so a 50-coin income still shows 1 coin. Alternative `round(a/100)` would make 1–49 invisible, which would be a worse regression than a slightly generous icon. Producer to confirm during plan/implement; code comment must document the chosen clamp.
- **Assumption: scope is income choreography only** — Sell/refund coin flies, `animateSell`, market deal-ins, and synergy formation are out of scope unless they also map coins 1:1. If they do, they are follow-up work items, not scope creep here.
- **Risk: rounding policy surprises** — `Math.round` vs. `Math.ceil` vs. `Math.floor` changes the feel for amounts like 150 (1 or 2 icons). Mitigation: use `Math.round` (nearest) and document; add a unit test that pins 150→2, 149→1, 50→1, 49→0-or-1 per the chosen clamp.
- **Risk: double-scaling** — Dividing both at grid creation and at collection would show 1 icon for 10,000 coins. Mitigation: scale once at icon creation; collection sweeps whatever is in the grid without re-dividing.
- **Scope-creep risk** — Temptation to add new SFX variants per 100, particle bursts per visual coin, or a dynamic divisor that scales with income size. Record as linked `discovered-from:CG-0MTK2JHXD004KNQI` work items; do not expand this bug's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the visual/SFX divisor be?" — Answer (operator, seed context): "1 per 100 (1 old coin = 100 new coins)." Source: work-item description for CG-0MTK2JHXD004KNQI (operator-provided, priority critical). No additional interview round was needed; the seed context is sufficient to draft a clear brief. Research: inspected `coin-grid.ts` (`splitCoins`, `packCoins`, `CoinGridHandle`), `MainStreetAnimator.ts` (`countOutCoins`, `flyCoinsIn`/`flyCoinsOut`, `collectIncomeGrids`, `creditedIncomeTotal`, `INCOME_*_STAGGER_MS`, `SFX_KEYS.COIN_POP`), `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` (`IncomeResult`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, `applyIncome`), and commit `192943c9` (×100 migration) — confirmed the phased income animation maps coin amount → icon/SFX 1:1, which is now 100× too dense.

*No open questions. The brief assumes `visualCount = max(1 for a>0, round(a/100))` vs. `round(a/100)` for 1–49 and legacy `animateIncomeCollection` alignment; confirm during plan/implement and document the chosen policy in code.*

# Fix card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting tests (CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH)

## Problem Statement

`192943c9` (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) migrated Main Street's economy to integers (×100) and updated the rendering/formatting helpers to integer-only output (`fmtRep` → `Math.round`, `formatTooltipDelta` → integer), but left the card-rendering, UI-overlay, and tooltip-formatting test suites asserting pre-migration fractional values (`+0.2/turn`, `Rep: +0.5`). This shard owns that cluster, which is currently 6 failures across 3–4 suites and blocks the parent `dev` green.

## Users

- **Build / release owner** — Needs `dev` green to unblock promotion to `main`; this shard is one of 10 shards under `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI`.
- **Main Street developers** — Need card-face SVGs, upgrade overlays, and tooltips to render integer economy values deterministically and to have tests that document the integer contract.

**User stories:**
- As a developer, I can run `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts tests/main-street/card-currency-formatting.test.ts` and see all tests pass with integer expectations reflecting the CSV/engine ×100 migration.
- As a player, I see consistent integer labels on card faces and overlays (`+20/turn`, `Rep: +50`, `Cash: +2 / -75`) with no spurious `.0` / `.000` decimals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` passes — all `reputationPerTurn`/`reputationBonus` fixtures scaled ×100 (e.g. `0.2` → `20`, `0.3` → `30`, `0.1` → `10`) and expected strings updated to integer form (`+20/turn`, `+30/turn`, `+10/turn`); `Integer reputation without decimal` and `fractional with one decimal` cases revised to cover integer formatting.
- [ ] `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` AC5 passes — `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` reputation text asserts integer form (`+30/turn` not `+0.3/turn`); no change to the two-tone `cashLine` contract required beyond fixture scaling if affected.
- [ ] `tests/main-street/card-currency-formatting.test.ts` — event tooltip (market, `includeEventDetail`) asserts integer `Rep: +50` (scaled from `+0.5`) and `Coins: +200` where applicable; `formatTooltipDelta` helpers verified to emit `+N` without `toFixed(3)` noise.
- [ ] `tests/main-street/event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts` fractional formatting case (if counted in this shard) updated to integer expectations — fractional `coinDelta: 2.5` → `250` with integer formatting, or the case is explicitly excluded and documented as owned by `CG-0MTKLQOL2007574V`.
- [ ] No engine/formatting regressions — `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.fmtRep`, `UpgradeOverlaySpec`, and `MainStreetFormatting.formatTooltipDelta` / `buildCardTooltipInfo` are unchanged except where a bug is proven; locale-aware `formatCurrency` remains the cost path.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Test-only change by default; do not revert the integer helpers (`fmtRep` `Math.round`, integer `formatTooltipDelta`) or reintroduce `toFixed(1/3)` paths.
- Preserve locale-aware currency formatting (`formatCurrency`) and synergy-rate display contracts; `synergyCoinBonus` / `multiplier` / `synergyRangeBonus` stay fractional rates.
- Follow `docs/DEVELOPER.md` quality gates: targeted `npx vitest run --project unit` for this shard during implementation, `npm run build` must pass before push.
- Do not edit `card-data.csv`, `csv-checksum.json`, or sibling shards' files.

## Existing State

- On `dev` HEAD (`192943c9` / `98a20e1e` → current `778f86dd`): `npm run build` passes; `npm test -- --project unit` shows 22 failed files / 79 failed tests (down from 65/296 after 5 shards landed). This shard's cluster accounts for:
  - `card-svg-generator.test.ts` (4 failures): expects `+0.2/turn`, `+0.3/turn`, `+0.1/turn`, `+0.3/turn` but receives `+0/turn` / `+1/turn` because `fmtRep` now rounds integers (`20` → `+20/turn`).
  - `cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (1 failure): AC5 expects `+0.3/turn` but engine emits `+0/turn` (fixture `0.3` with integer rounding).
  - `card-currency-formatting.test.ts` (1 failure): expects `Rep: +0.5` but receives `Rep: +1` (fixture `0.5` should be `50` → `+50`).
  - `event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts` (1 adjacent failure in the overall 22, `fractional coinDelta` with `toFixed`): `CoinDelta 2.5` → `250`; owned ambiguously — clarify in this intake whether it belongs here or to `CG-0MTKLQOL2007574V`.
- Engine helpers already integer-only: `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.fmtRep(v)` returns `String(Math.round(v))`; `UpgradeOverlaySpec` formats `totalReputation` via `Math.round`; `MainStreetFormatting.formatTooltipDelta` rounds and strips decimals.
- Parent `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI` is `plan_complete` with 10 child shards; 5 are `completed/in_review`, 1 is `in_progress` (`CG-0MTKLPTJP003HDA0`), this item and two others are `idea`/`open`.

## Desired Change

- Update the card rendering, UI overlay, and formatting test suites to the ×100 integer contract:
  - Scale all coin/reputation fixtures ×100 (`reputationPerTurn`, `reputationBonus`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `ongoingCost` where applicable) via `Math.round(old * 100)`.
  - Update expected strings to integer form (`+20/turn`, `+50`, `+250` etc.) and remove or rewrite the `one-decimal` / `toFixed(1/3)` assertion branches to assert `no spurious decimals` instead.
  - Keep `income` / `cost` badge assertions locale-agnostic (`>€N<` / `Cost: €N`) and synergy display unchanged.
  - Document shard boundary: if `event-card-tooltip-info` fractional case belongs to the CSV-pipeline shard, note the exclusion in a code comment and in the work-item comment.
- No production code change expected; if a helper is found to mis-round scaled integers, file a blocking bug (`blocked-by:`) rather than expanding scope.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — Scale `reputationPerTurn`/`reputationBonus` fixtures ×100; update `+0.x/turn` expectations to `+Nx/turn`; rewrite formatting section to assert integer.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — Scale `reputationPerTurn` fixture in AC5 (`0.3` → `30`) and update `+0.3/turn` → `+30/turn`.
- `tests/main-street/card-currency-formatting.test.ts` — Scale `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta` fixtures (e.g. `0.5` → `50`, `2` → `200`); update `Rep: +0.5` → `Rep: +50` expectation; keep `formatCurrency` locale tests.
- `tests/main-street/event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts` — (Boundary) Update or explicitly exclude fractional `coinDelta: 2.5` case; integer economy uses `250`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Reference only; `fmtRep` already `Math.round`, do not revert.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — Reference only; `repFormatted` already `Math.round`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Reference only; `formatTooltipDelta` already integer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Type reference for `reputationPerTurn` / `reputationBonus` scaling context.

## Related Work

- **Parent:** `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI` — Fix integer economy test breakage — update expectations to ×100 values (`plan_complete`, `critical`)
- **Siblings (5 landed):** `CG-0MTKLOGM7000DMAA` (`completed/in_review`), `CG-0MTKLOQHS000Q4NB` (`completed/in_review`), `CG-0MTKLOZVG00513BO` (`completed/in_review`), `CG-0MTKLP9K1001BBEE` (`completed/in_review`), `CG-0MTKLPKBS008EQ4Q` (`completed/in_review` — 14 suites, 295 tests, ×100)
- **Siblings (in-progress/open):** `CG-0MTKLPTJP003HDA0` (`in_progress`), `CG-0MTKLQ9P9007G5BM` (`open`), `CG-0MTKLQGYZ002Y476` (`open`), `CG-0MTKLQOL2007574V` (`open` — boundary for `event-card-tooltip-info` / CSV pipeline)
- **Root cause:** `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — Move to integer numbers for coins and reputation (`completed`) — commit `192943c9` migrated `card-data.csv`/engine to ×100 and updated only `coin-grid.test.ts` + `reputation-coin-multiplier.test.ts`
- **Potentially related docs:** `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`, `src/core-engine/I18n.ts` (`formatCurrency`), `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (quality gates / test profiles)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** `fmtRep` / `UpgradeOverlaySpec` integer rounding is the intended contract (per `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6`); tests must follow the engine, not the reverse — if review disagrees, the risk is reintroducing fractional display.
- **Risk — Shard boundary creep:** `event-card-tooltip-info` fractional case could be double-owned with `CG-0MTKLQOL2007574V`; mitigation: declare ownership in this brief and record a `Blocked-by:`/`Related-to:` comment if deferred.
- **Risk — Hidden locale/polish:** `card-currency-formatting` locale-switch tests use `formatCurrency`; mitigation: keep symbol assertions (`€` / `$`) unchanged and do not hardcode decimals.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Requests to re-tune visual layout (icon placement, cash-line two-tone) or to re-scale `synergyCoinBonus` rates are out of scope — record as `discovered-from:CG-0MTKLQ1P40091YTH` work items instead.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What is the source of truth for the ×100 scaling in this shard?" — Answer (repo evidence): `192943c9` migrated `card-data.csv` (`cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `synergyRepBonus`, `ongoingCost`, `incomeBonus`, `reputationBonus`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`) ×100 and helpers to `Math.round`; `git show 192943c9 --stat` and the five landed sibling commits (`e6872e97`, `3fd6cbe8`, `3d9a6cb8`, `778f86dd`) establish the ×100 + integer-rounding contract. Source: `git show 192943c9` + `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts:fmtRep` / `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts:repFormatted` / `MainStreetFormatting.ts:formatTooltipDelta`.
- Q: "Does this shard change production code?" — Answer (agent assessment, no producer input required): No by default — `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`, `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`, and `MainStreetFormatting.ts` already emit integers; only test fixtures/expectations are updated. Any helper bug discovered becomes a `blocked-by:` item. Source: file reads in this intake session.
- Q: "Where does `event-card-tooltip-info`'s fractional `coinDelta: 2.5` belong?" — Answer (open, producer to confirm): Tentatively in this shard if the tooltip is treated as formatting, otherwise in `CG-0MTKLQOL2007574V` (CSV pipeline & event tooltip). The brief records the boundary; intake will add a `Related-to:` comment linking the two items and the chosen owner will close the loop. Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — needs producer review if both shards claim it.

## Problem Statement

`192943c9` (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6) migrated Main Street's economy to integers (×100) and rounded `applyReputationMultiplier` via `roundInt`, but left `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`, `save-load.test.ts`, `checkpoint-manager.test.ts`, and `graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` asserting pre-migration fractional values and stale coin/reputation cushions. This shard owns that cluster — currently **18 failures / 91 tests** across the 4 suites — and blocks parent `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI` from going green.

## Users

- **Build / release owner** — Needs `dev` green (`npm run build` + unit suite) to unblock promotion to `main` and to surface the next real ENOSPC/monte-carlo issue without noise; this is shard 8 of 10 under `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI`.
- **Main Street developers** — Need turn-flow, persistence, and incident-card contracts to document the ×100 integer economy deterministically so future CSV/engine changes are caught by tests, not by players.

Verified by `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts tests/main-street/checkpoint-manager.test.ts`.

Verified by `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/graffiti-art-incident.test.ts`.
- [ ] No engine/CSV changes — `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` (`computeScore`, `applyReputationMultiplier`/`roundInt`), `MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`, `MainStreetCards.ts` (`CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`, `STARTING_COINS`, `card-data.csv` rows `evt-graffiti`/`evt-graffiti-art`) and `src/core-engine` checkpoint helpers are unchanged except for comments if needed; only test fixtures/expectations are updated.

- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm run build` passes; `npx vitest run --project unit` green for this shard's 4 suites and no new browser regressions for these files).

## Constraints

- Test-only change by default; do not revert the integer helpers (`CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS 1000`, `applyReputationMultiplier` `roundInt`, `fmtRep` `Math.round`) or reintroduce fractional/`toFixed` paths.

- If a helper is found to mis-round scaled integers, file a `blocked-by:` bug rather than expanding scope.

## Existing State

- On `dev` HEAD (base `98a20e1e` + landed shards through `778f86dd`): `npm run build` passes; `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts tests/main-street/checkpoint-manager.test.ts tests/main-street/graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` shows **4 failed files / 18 failed tests / 73 passed** (repro at 2026-09-03):
  - `turnflow.test.ts` (12 failures): `computeScore 80 → 2060`, `updateScore 115 → 1105`, `buy-business Need 400 have 100`, `buy-upgrade Need 300 have 100`, `play-event/resolveEvent 4.15→4` / `5.1875→5` / `3.1125→3` integer rounding, `executeFullTurn`/`multi-turn Need 400/800/1200 have 100/50`, `challenge EndCheck ch-deep-pockets false` (100 < 3000).

  - `checkpoint-manager.test.ts` (1 failure): `save/load round-trip preserves turn-start state — Not enough coins. Need 500, have 100`.
  - `graffiti-art-incident.test.ts` (4 failures): contract `reputationDelta '1' vs '100'`, deck `reputationDelta 1 vs 100`, resolution `repBefore + 1 vs +100`, mirror `coinsBefore - 1 vs -100` (`500 vs 599` at `STARTING_COINS=600`).
- Engine already integer-only: `MainStreetCards.ts:CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS = 1000`, `STARTING_COINS = 600`, `card-data.csv` `evt-graffiti -100/-100`, `evt-graffiti-art 0/100`; `MainStreetDifficulty.ts:applyReputationMultiplier` rounds via `roundInt`; `MainStreetEngine.ts:computeScore` syncs via `EconomyLedger`.
- Parent `CG-0MTK38DA20099NCI` is `plan_complete` with 10 child shards; 5 are `completed/in_review`, 2 `in_progress`/`intake_complete`, 3 `plan_complete`/`idea` including this item (`idea`).

## Desired Change

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — Scale `computeScore`/`updateScore` bonus to `1000`, bump coin cushions `100→1000`, bump `ch-deep-pockets` to `3000`, round event deltas to integer (`4.15→4` etc.)
